chapters.title: Chapter 126: Holy Trinity
paragraphs: "... Fine! It will be a closed re-testing with only you, me, and the four youngsters present. All findings will be kept entirely off-record."

’She started with China, continued with India, and now to finish off the Holy Trinity of nations that pose the gravest threat to our country...’ Grace excitedly awaited Vespera’s response as her mind raced with possibilities of what she might say next. ’What nonsense would this woman dare utter on official government line?!’ she screamed inwardly with excitement.

"Chairman, we still found no leads on the connection between the Russian terrorist who made an attempt on the president’s life and his home country. As a loyal citizen of the United States, the recent days have been extremely trying on my mental well-being. I feel I’m not doing my duty unless I travel there in person and conduct a thorough investigation myself. Vladimir himself invited me to do so. Though, he also said he wanted to show me his great country once I concluded they had nothing to do with it, so it might take a while for me to return."
’There it is, the Holy Trinity has been completed!’ Grace giggled inwardly just as...
*Crack!* *Snap!* *Thud!*

Numerous veins bulged on the chairman’s arms as he outright tore the second armrest off of his chair and threw it to the ground. His frustration was palpable, and the sound of the armrest shattering mirrored the growing tension in the room.
"It seems you’re in the middle of something. I’ll leave you to it," Vespera said and terminated the communication line without waiting for his response.
It took an entire minute for the chairman to calm himself. Grace dutifully stood still like a statue while waiting for her boss to either dismiss her or...

"So, Miss Grace, as the person tasked with observing this lovely woman’s son, did you catch something meaningful that might’ve flown by my ears without notice?" Sarcasm was present in his tone as he referenced Grace’s earlier words when she asked him to put Vespera on speaker mode.
She completely ignored his tone and smiled brightly, "Sir, I believe Vespera Ashborn isn’t very fond of you, and she might betray her country should we mess with her son."
"... Thank you for the acute observation, Miss Grace."
"Phew! This grinding session was an outright soul-cleansing experience!" Nyx decreed with a toothy grin while wiping the sweat from her forehead with her arm.

"We should do this more often. I think this is the push you need to begin losing your enormous fat reserves," Luna said while eyeing Nyx’s heavily heaving cleavage in particular with a strong frown evident on her delicate face.
"Bestie, you should ask Kai whether he wants me to lose weight or not."

The two hissing kittens turned their heads in the man’s direction, only to see him lying on the dungeon’s ground on his stomach with Aria seated on his back. She was in the middle of giving him a back massage. They spent the last few hours grinding nonstop, so they concluded the stream and walked back to the entrance where danger wasn’t present, letting them relax before retiring for the day.
"... The princess is a cunning opportunist..." Nyx murmured.

"Her kind exterior makes one think she’s a harmless creature, but in reality, she’s a ruthless predator, always ready to pounce as soon as the opportunity presents itself," Luna voiced her agreement for once as she eyed Aria with the gaze of a woman who was measuring her competition up.
"Kai, you were very cool today!" Aria cheered while using her trained arms to knead his shoulder blades, eliciting minor groans of pleasure from her man.
"Thanks, but you three were today’s stars."
"Hehe! You say that, but you still killed more monsters than any of us!"
"Is that so..." Kaiden whispered while opening his status window to observe today’s enormous gains.
[Name: Kaiden Grey]
[Rank: 2 - Budding Star]
[Class: Paragon of Sin]
[Stats]
{Vitality: 15 → 23}
{Strength: 18 → 26}
{Agility: 17 → 25}
{Endurance: 17 → 25}
{Mana: 10}
{Magic: 10}
[Views: 1.29 million → 1.35 million]
[Fangirls: 103 → 106]
[Sinsworn Valkyries]
< Luna Aster >
< Aria Levander >
< Nyx Cosmos >
[Skills]
1. [Silent Casting] (???-tier)
2. [Monster Girl Subjugator] (S-tier)
3. [Adaptive Reflexes] (B-tier)
4. [Immune Cock] (D-tier)
5. [Harem Vision] (D-tier)
6. [Remove Her Inhibitions] (E-tier)

His system’s three unique stats, namely views, fangirls, and income didn’t see much increase because Kaiden didn’t upload any adult content for two days. He had spent yesterday fighting thugs to free Julia, and today was dungeon day. He didn’t mind, though. Some downtime was perfect to let the audience’s eagerness increase for their next release... alongside the fattening of their wallets.
And yes, in a single day, he went from level 3 to 7. It was an incredibly successful day. The four of them worked in tandem as they continuously polished their teamwork.

However, the issue with this dungeon was beginning to bear its ugly fangs at Kaiden and co. He gained 36 stat points, which meant he averaged a little more than 8 per level—which he spread evenly across the four physical stats, thinking them to be equally important to him right now.

While ~8 stat points/level were admirable gains, Kaiden couldn’t help but be a bit disappointed after getting 10 for his first level-up. The reason for his lower gains could be chalked up to the dungeon and its simplicity.

This was the perfect beginner dungeon because the monsters were all rather simple beasts. The mushroom creepers were the rare minority of more complicated monsters one could meet here, most were just evolved animals.
This meant that their simplicity lowered their difficulty, which in turn lowered the gains he got for slaying them.
Then why not just go deeper into the dungeon to meet stronger monsters?
First of all, as an F-rank dungeon, even the monsters on the edges of the dimension weren’t incredibly strong. Even spotting a single level 20 monster would be rare.

Second, there was a cap on what was reasonable. They were already hunting for monsters that were above them in level, but if they ventured too far, they could chance upon high-leveled monsters that were simply impossible for them to fight due to the vast stat difference between them.

On average, monsters already had higher stats than an awakened of the same level, and this further increased for beast-type monsters—the specialty of this dungeon. Therefore, if they dared to venture too far, a level 20 monster might jump them. They likely couldn’t even injure a beast-type monster of that level as they were right now; it would simply have too high defenses thanks to its overwhelming Vitality stat.
*Chime!*

A sound he had never heard before sounded in Kaiden’s mind all of a sudden, making him flinch out of reflex and glance around, looking for enemies. However, he soon realized that it was the sound of none other than his awakened platform notifying him of an awakened person sending him a personal message for the first time in his life.
Although Kaiden didn’t know it yet, this unexpected message would completely alter his future by giving him the opportunity of a lifetime!

"So, Miss Grace, as the person tasked with observing this lovely woman’s son, did you catch something meaningful that might’ve flown by my ears without notice?" Sarcasm was present in his tone as he referenced Grace’s earlier words when she asked him to put Vespera on speaker mode.
She completely ignored his tone and smiled brightly, "Sir, I believe Vespera Ashborn isn’t very fond of you, and she might betray her country should we mess with her son."
Thank you for the acute observation, Miss Grace."
"Phew!
This grinding session was an outright soul-cleansing experience!" Nyx decreed with a toothy grin while wiping the sweat from her forehead with her arm.
"We should do this more often.
I think this is the push you need to begin losing your enormous fat reserves," Luna said while eyeing Nyx’s heavily heaving cleavage in particular with a strong frown evident on her delicate face.
"Bestie, you should ask Kai whether he wants me to lose weight or not."
The two hissing kittens turned their heads in the man’s direction, only to see him lying on the dungeon’s ground on his stomach with Aria seated on his back.
She was in the middle of giving him a back massage.
They spent the last few hours grinding nonstop, so they concluded the stream and walked back to the entrance where danger wasn’t present, letting them relax before retiring for the day.
The princess is a cunning opportunist..." Nyx murmured.

"Her kind exterior makes one think she’s a harmless creature, but in reality, she’s a ruthless predator, always ready to pounce as soon as the opportunity presents itself," Luna voiced her agreement for once as she eyed Aria with the gaze of a woman who was measuring her competition up.
"Kai, you were very cool today!" Aria cheered while using her trained arms to knead his shoulder blades, eliciting minor groans of pleasure from her man.
"Thanks, but you three were today’s stars."
"Hehe!
You say that, but you still killed more monsters than any of us!"
"Is that so..." Kaiden whispered while opening his status window to observe today’s enormous gains.
[Name: Kaiden Grey]
[Rank: 2 - Budding Star]
[Class: Paragon of Sin]
[Stats]
{Vitality: 15 → 23}
{Strength: 18 → 26}
{Agility: 17 → 25}
{Endurance: 17 → 25}
{Mana: 10}
{Magic: 10}
[Views: 1.29 million → 1.35 million]
[Fangirls: 103 → 106]
[Sinsworn Valkyries]
< Luna Aster >
< Aria Levander >
< Nyx Cosmos >
[Skills]
[Silent Casting] (???-tier)
[Monster Girl Subjugator] (S-tier)
[Adaptive Reflexes] (B-tier)
[Immune Cock] (D-tier)
[Harem Vision] (D-tier)
[Remove Her Inhibitions] (E-tier)
His system’s three unique stats, namely views, fangirls, and income didn’t see much increase because Kaiden didn’t upload any adult content for two days.
He had spent yesterday fighting thugs to free Julia, and today was dungeon day.
He didn’t mind, though.
Some downtime was perfect to let the audience’s eagerness increase for their next release... alongside the fattening of their wallets.
And yes, in a single day, he went from level 3 to 7.
It was an incredibly successful day.
The four of them worked in tandem as they continuously polished their teamwork.
However, the issue with this dungeon was beginning to bear its ugly fangs at Kaiden and co.
He gained 36 stat points, which meant he averaged a little more than 8 per level—which he spread evenly across the four physical stats, thinking them to be equally important to him right now.
While ~8 stat points/level were admirable gains, Kaiden couldn’t help but be a bit disappointed after getting 10 for his first level-up.
The reason for his lower gains could be chalked up to the dungeon and its simplicity.
This was the perfect beginner dungeon because the monsters were all rather simple beasts.
The mushroom creepers were the rare minority of more complicated monsters one could meet here, most were just evolved animals.
This meant that their simplicity lowered their difficulty, which in turn lowered the gains he got for slaying them.
Then why not just go deeper into the dungeon to meet stronger monsters?
First of all, as an F-rank dungeon, even the monsters on the edges of the dimension weren’t incredibly strong.
Even spotting a single level 20 monster would be rare.
Second, there was a cap on what was reasonable.

They were already hunting for monsters that were above them in level, but if they ventured too far, they could chance upon high-leveled monsters that were simply impossible for them to fight due to the vast stat difference between them.
On average, monsters already had higher stats than an awakened of the same level, and this further increased for beast-type monsters—the specialty of this dungeon.
Therefore, if they dared to venture too far, a level 20 monster might jump them.
They likely couldn’t even injure a beast-type monster of that level as they were right now; it would simply have too high defenses thanks to its overwhelming Vitality stat.
*Chime!*
A sound he had never heard before sounded in Kaiden’s mind all of a sudden, making him flinch out of reflex and glance around, looking for enemies.
However, he soon realized that it was the sound of none other than his awakened platform notifying him of an awakened person sending him a personal message for the first time in his life.
Although Kaiden didn’t know it yet, this unexpected message would completely alter his future by giving him the opportunity of a lifetime!

chapters.title: Chapter 127: Nova Circuit
paragraphs: - Tessa: Dear Kaiden, I’m Tessa, guild leader of Nova Circuit. A scout of ours saw the might your team displayed today, and I must say, it left quite an impression. I’d like to offer you a proposition. Would you be able to meet in person shortly?

Kaiden reread it just to make sure his eyes weren’t deceiving him. Were they scouted already? While clearing a beginner dungeon? It made him feel good but also a bit strange. He thought this might be fishy, so he looked up the sender and her guild.

Tessa was a B-tier awakened with an estimated level of 55-70, with the class Arcane Archer. ’Arcane’ was a highly favored subtype of an archetype; it referred to their ability to fight with energy-based attacks, explosions, lasers, and the like.
David also had the Arcane subtype, though he was an Archmage and not an Archer, making his class superior—hence his A-tier assessment.
As for the guild she led, Nova Circuit, it was a low-tier one. Guilds could be categorized into three broad tiers: low, mid, and high.
What separated the tiers was the quality of their members and their ability to clear dungeons effectively. Funding, prestige, and leadership also played pivotal roles in determining a guild’s tier.

Nova Circuit used to be mid-tier, but they fell back to low-tier. Kaiden didn’t know what had happened as the info he found on them didn’t go into specifics, but a lot of their strongest members decided to leave and join another guild. Perhaps internal conflict or mismanagement had caused the decline.
- Kaiden: Dear Tessa, thank you for reaching out, but we’re not interested in joining any guild right now.

He decided to decline her gently, not because her guild was low-tier but because he didn’t lie when he said he had no intention of joining any guild. Depending on the contract, a guild could even demand a portion of his earnings from his adult videos, making it harder for him to increase the income statistic of the system. That was assuming they don’t outright forbid him from uploading adult content in the first place.
- Tessa: I’m sad to hear that, but I didn’t reach out to you with the intention of recruitment.
- Kiaden: Then?
- Tessa: I’m sorry, but I would like to hold this conversation face-to-face. Since it’s me who is being so difficult, I’ll travel to your choice of meeting place, should you be willing to meet.
Kaiden quickly discussed the news with his girls, and together, they decided to entertain this woman. It wasn’t every day that a guild leader came knocking unprompted, after all.
"A cappuccino for me, please," Kaiden ordered from the cute waitress.
"Hot chocolate."
"I’ll take an espresso."
"May I have a caramel oat milk latte, topped with a sprinkle of cinnamon sugar?"
"Most certainly!" the waitress cheered, after which she departed to deliver their orders.
Luna and Nyx, who ordered after Kaiden, eyed Aria curiously due to her choice of drink.
"It’s the first time in my life I can afford to get something fancy like this. Stop looking at me like I’m a soulless Inst*gram influencer!" Aria scoffed; she was very defensive.
"True, it’s the fat bimbo who keeps posting pictures nonstop," Luna agreed.

"I’m the social media manager of Valhalla’s Sinners, so it’s my job, but I digress. Instead, let me voice my surprise; you two managed to sit down at a table as if you were normal people instead of climbing all over Kai. The chaos gremlin didn’t place her little butt on his lap while the Disn*y princess didn’t start holding his hand as if they were glued together."

As soon as the words left Nyx’s tantalizing lips, Aria subconsciously reached her hand toward Kaiden’s before she caught herself, and a rosy pink shade emerged on her cheeks, realizing just how right the Space Valkyrie’s assessment of her tendencies ended up being. Luna, meanwhile, began glaring daggers at the woman, but before she could part her lips to most certainly deliver a very unladylike response, Kaiden successfully intervened, placating the ladies. It didn’t take long for the waitress to deliver their requested drinks.
"Not a soulless Instagram influencer, huh." Nyx giggled slyly as she saw Aria immediately begin taking pictures of her fancy coffee immediately.
"I’m sending it to Mom!" Aria defended herself. "She must be so bored..."

Julia was still in the hospital, but she was making a quick recovery. The Levander mother no longer needed infusion because her condition had stabilized. She might be allowed to go home at any moment now. Until then, Julia busied herself by following her daughter’s awakened journey and chatting with her younger daughter, Lux, who visited her a lot.

Naturally, what she watched of Aria’s awakened journey didn’t include the adult parts, such as the one where she was pretending to be a slutty nurse and getting ravaged by Kaiden’s throbbing 9 incher.
"Ah, you’re here."

A voice sounded from next to them, and when Kaiden turned his head in its direction, he was greeted by a black-haired woman who had big blue eyes. She wore a form-fitting white turtleneck that accentuated her generous, feminine figure.

Kaiden saw pictures of Tessa when he did a quick search on her, but she was always in her combat attire in those pictures. Here, she looked very fashionable—so much so that it took him a few seconds to realize that it was the same woman as the one in the pictures.
He stood to greet her properly. It was a business meeting, after all. The three Valkyries did the same.
Once the five of them were seated, it was time to begin.
"Miss Tessa, I’m truly curious about your reason for being so secretive during our chat on the awakened platform."

She wryly smiled in response. "I’m an old-fashioned woman who would rather spend two hours traveling to meet in person than to speak over the phone... or the awakened platform in this case. I must seem like a weird woman to you youngsters."
"Aren’t you like 28 or something?" Luna deadpanned.
"Don’t even get me started..." Tessa sighed with exhaustion before continuing, "However, that’s just my preference. For talks like this, speaking in person is the normal thing to do."
"But for ’talks like this,’ it would not be the guild leader who comes personally to speak with four low-level, low-tier awakened," Nyx countered.
"... You’re right," Tessa admitted. "Truth be told, I need your help. We need to clear a dungeon that has a very annoying restriction: those who are level 10 or above can’t enter."
A giant grin emerged on Kaiden’s face for a moment before he suppressed it. His plan was already working.
As stated before, there were two ways he could gain access to uncharted dungeons. One, make a guild and pay insane sums, as even the registration itself costs an arm and a leg, or two, join a guild.

However, there was a third option, a crafty, high-risk, high-reward one: remain independent and low-level while broadcasting his competence, where a desperate guild might reach out to them in the exact case Nova Circuit seems to have found itself in.
"You can’t clear it with your low-level members, so you need help from competent outsiders," Nyx voiced her thoughts.

chapters.title: Chapter 128: Duties of Official Guilds
paragraphs: One might be confused regarding how a guild could find themselves in this circumstance in the first place; after all, if they don’t have promising rookies, they just shouldn’t buy the contract for the dungeon from the association.

The issue arose from the duties of official guilds. While it was true that the standard process was guilds paying for exclusive access to dungeons, it was not the only way they could gain entry into one.

The second method was to be instructed by the association to clear it. The contract between guilds and the association stated that the latter could give a dungeon to the former, which had to be cleared. Naturally, such dungeons were the ones that had annoying clear conditions and were evaluated as ’too much trouble for little return,’ and as a result, no guild wanted to buy it from the association.

Dungeon gates were not just mere portals connecting two different dimensions but also acted as restrictors. Some dungeons had an entrance limit where the maximum number of awakened who could enter was lowered, others had level limits, class archetype limits, weapon or artifact limits, and the like. These restrictions were often randomized, forcing guilds to adapt or fail.

These dungeons could be bought for cheap, but if no guild went for them, then the association would force it upon guilds. Each guild tier, namely low, mid, and high, had to accept and clear a different number of forced dungeons each year. Failing to do so was one of the easiest ways for a guild to fall to lower tiers. Guilds that couldn’t fulfill their assigned quota faced audits, budget cuts, or even dissolution in extreme cases.
However, as Nova Circuit was already a low-tier one, the penalty for them would be to lose their full rights as a guild. They would either have to merge with another guild or get absolved.
All that is to say, Guild status wasn’t merely a title; it came with responsibilities, obligations, and a constant pressure to prove their usefulness to the association.
"That’s right..." Tessa nodded in response to Nyx’s observation.

She sighed dejectedly before explaining, "Our guild fell upon dire times, we’re struggling with recruiting promising rookies. There’s only a single A-tier awakened in our midst, and she’s eligible to enter the dungeon, but her presence won’t be enough to clear the dungeon, I fear.

We can’t afford to pay for the help of other guilds, while asking for help from the association would mean we failed to clear it and get penalized, so our best bet is to search the country for independent awakened who happen to be below level 10. One of my scouts saw your stream, and she estimated that you had to be around levels 5 and 9, which made you prime candidates for us to reach out to."
"Your scout estimated correctly. What’s the dungeon’s difficulty rating?" Kaiden asked.
"It’s a D-rank dungeon."
That was a two-rank jump from the F-rank dungeon they had experienced thus far. It explained why the low-level A-ranked awakened wasn’t believed to be enough to clear it.
"Have you sent an exploration party in?" This time around, it was Aria who asked the question.

"Yes, a sandy biome awaits inside, and the main enemy types seem to be scarabs, desert felines, and mummies. Our goal is to organize a party consisting of around twenty awakened, sixteen of which are our guild members, but we felt our forces to be insufficient."

If sixteen people were not sufficient for a D-rank dungeon, that likely meant they had very few high tiers among them. By reaching out to outsiders, the guild admitted to its weakness, so it was a last resort. Thus, Kaiden thought they must firmly believe that their forces stand almost no chance at success.

It was recommended that the average of an awakened group that enters a dungeon should be at least one tier above that of the dungeon’s rank to clear with acceptable casualty figures. Therefore, 16 people who averaged C-tier among their ranks should be more than enough to clear it, making it almost certain their members were mostly low-tiers.
"You do realize we’re F-tiers, right?" Luna spoke up while eyeing Tessa.

"I did my research on you four while I was traveling here. I’m aware. I don’t know how you got that assessment, but I’m confident it was the result of a malfunction. But even if it’s right, it doesn’t matter to me. All I care about is that you’re incredibly competent for low levels, the exact type of people our expedition force needs to bolster its ranks."
"If you’d done your homework diligently, then you would also know we’re not just combatants. Is that no problem for you?" Nyx asked tactfully.

Tessa nodded. "I know of your adult videos and other non-combat content. You’re right in that I normally wouldn’t want to associate my guild with your brand, but the more I saw of your dungeon clears, the more I thought that you four are something special, which made me reconsider. We had a few more outsiders who were in consideration, but I was adamant about reaching out to you four first. I can’t explain it well, just that my senses were telling me to go with you. Call it a risky investment if you will," she finished with a friendly smile.

"If we accept, do you consent to us broadcasting the clear and then uploading an edited video to our platform?" Kaiden inquired. It was a unique chance to make his combat-oriented content more varied. After today, they would have two clears of the F-rank forest biome dungeon. He wanted to switch things up, and there were not many things more exciting than an unexplored, fresh dungeon.

"Yes. When a guild reaches out to outsiders for help, it’s customary to treat them as mercenaries, and mercenaries don’t work for free. I’m ashamed to say our finances are in the deep red, I can’t pay you in the literal sense. My proposal is as follows: I’ll provide you with written consent to broadcast the dungeon descent, ensuring you retain all rights to any revenue generated from it. Furthermore, you’ll be eligible for one-third of all the loot found during the duration of the expedition, including monster drops, mined minerals, and valuables found in chests."

It was a weak offer, considering the trouble Nova Circuit was in. Mercs were usually paid a down payment before even setting foot into a dungeon, and guilds typically offered additional compensation for career-ending injuries or death. Still, Kaiden wasn’t dismayed. His main goal had always been to gain access to a dungeon like this; getting paid as well would’ve merely been the cream on top.

"Have you estimated how much time we have to prepare for the clear?" If a dungeon wasn’t cleared within a certain timeframe, a dungeon break would occur, allowing the monsters to spill out through the gates and invade Earth. The window for clearing a dungeon before a break was unpredictable, varying greatly from one to another, but the association possessed artifacts capable of measuring it.
Tessa had an ashen, embarrassed expression as she replied, "... Until tomorrow morning."

When a guild reaches out to outsiders for help, it’s customary to treat them as mercenaries, and mercenaries don’t work for free.
I’m ashamed to say our finances are in the deep red, I can’t pay you in the literal sense.
My proposal is as follows: I’ll provide you with written consent to broadcast the dungeon descent, ensuring you retain all rights to any revenue generated from it.
Furthermore, you’ll be eligible for one-third of all the loot found during the duration of the expedition, including monster drops, mined minerals, and valuables found in chests."
It was a weak offer, considering the trouble Nova Circuit was in.
Mercs were usually paid a down payment before even setting foot into a dungeon, and guilds typically offered additional compensation for career-ending injuries or death.
Still, Kaiden wasn’t dismayed.
His main goal had always been to gain access to a dungeon like this; getting paid as well would’ve merely been the cream on top.

"Have you estimated how much time we have to prepare for the clear?" If a dungeon wasn’t cleared within a certain timeframe, a dungeon break would occur, allowing the monsters to spill out through the gates and invade Earth.
The window for clearing a dungeon before a break was unpredictable, varying greatly from one to another, but the association possessed artifacts capable of measuring it.
Tessa had an ashen, embarrassed expression as she replied, "...
Until tomorrow morning."

chapters.title: Chapter 129: Meeting the Team
paragraphs: "Kai, I’m not sure how to feel about this all..." Aria murmured.

It was the next day, which meant the dungeon descent would take place today. They had five days until a dungeon break would occur, but the Awakened Association guidelines stated that a guild has to clear its dungeons 48 hours before the estimated deadline. If they couldn’t achieve that, then it would be counted as a failure, and the association would take it upon itself to assemble a team that was good enough to clear it in two days. They would do so either by using their internal agents or making the awakened of official guilds do it for them in exchange for rewards.
This was the protocol for the F, E, and D-ranked dungeons. Higher ranks required more time to clear, so the guilds had to complete the dungeons faster before the association would step in.
"It’ll be fine. We’re ready for the D rank."

"Based on what do you say this, Mr. Confident?" Luna asked with an amused tone. The four of them were sitting in the back of a minivan. Due to their combat equipment, a smaller ride wouldn’t have been sufficient this time around.
Considering Kaiden and co were low-levels who only ever entered a beginner-friendly F-ranked dungeon, the Storm Valkyrie was more than justified in calling him out on his BS.

Kaiden knew it as well, best evidenced by his decision to steer the conversation in his preferred direction, earning himself a cute scoff in the process. "I wonder how the rest of our team will be. They should’ve gotten some training from the more experienced members of their guild. Maybe we’ll get to learn some tricks from them."

"It’s standard procedure for rookie awakened to be trained by the guild they join for years before they’re sent on their first dangerous mission. However, Tessa’s lack of confidence is all we need to know, I think," Nyx said. "She wouldn’t have embarrassed herself by approaching us otherwise. We’re her last hope."
"Us... You’re saying it like we’re the plague." Luna didn’t appreciate Nyx’s tone.

"Well, the recording of your coochie is on the platform, alongside your shower blowjob, bestie. Mr. Confident over here got disowned over this ’small issue.’ No respectable guild would want to associate themselves with our brand."

"At least not until we become too big to ignore!" Aria cheered, lightening the tense mood that seemed to always surround the two fierce kittens. Even though she and Kaiden were sitting between the two, they still found ways to fight.

"That’s right. We just have to do our own thing. We’re trying to do something unprecedented over here by traversing uncharted waters. It’s only natural that we’re being looked down upon until we prove our approach works. It’s the trendsetters who have to pave the way, but they’re also the ones who reap the most benefits for their bravery to innovate and try new things," Kaiden said while putting his arm over Aria’s and Nyx’s backs, resting it on their shoulders. The two beauties happily nestled their head against his shoulder, which did not help improve the sole woman’s mood who wasn’t sitting next to Kaiden.
With that, the squad chatted away the remainder of the two-hour-long journey. Once the minivan parked at their destination, they got out and came face to face with an imposing guild headquarters.
Nova Circuit might’ve been demoted to the status of a low-tier guild, but they were once a mid-tier organization, and it showed. Their building was prestigious.

Its exterior was made of dark-tinted glass and reinforced steel, with neon-blue circuit-like patterns running along its surface, strongly hinting at the founder’s favoritism toward the Arcane subclass category.

Though some areas showed signs of wear, this building still exuded power. Owning such a guild HQ was not just about comfort and luxury: it was a statement of strength. Getting recruits to sign up if they got to live and train in such a unique building would be easier, while other guilds wouldn’t look down on them for being cheap.
Kaiden and his Valkyries made their way toward the automatic sliding doors placed under a massive holographic sign that displayed the guild’s emblem, which was a vividly streaking comet.

The inside was just as luxurious as the outside. It was spacious and filled with mementos of the guild’s rich past. Many paintings detailed their history, though most works seemed to be made years ago, during the guild’s golden era.

They strolled to the reception desk, where a woman welcomed them. She gasped upon laying her eyes on the squad, but Kaiden didn’t pay it much heed. He placed their awakened identifications on her table and said, "I’m Kaiden Gray, and these ladies are my teammates, Luna, Aria, and Nyx. We’re mercenaries guild leader Tessa brought here to help the guild clear a D-ranked dungeon."
"I’d been informed..." she muttered while stealing shy glances at him.
"Please turn right and walk until you reach the end of the corridor, then take a left..." the receptionist said after registering them in the guild’s system.
As soon as they were out of earshot, the Valkyries burst into amused snickers.
"A fangirl, huh," Kaiden said upon witnessing their reactions. He wasn’t socially inept enough not to see how flustered the woman was.
"Duh. She must’ve been told by staff to expect us, and out of curiosity, she searched for info regarding the mercenaries her guild hired," Luna revealed her thoughts, accompanied by a giant grin.
"And during her little research, one click led to another, and she soon found herself face to face with Mr. Confident and his throbbing lance..." Nyx purred.
"I wonder if it was my nurse play?" Aria asked bashfully, a pink shade adorned her cheeks.
"That was the video that brought in by far the most fangirls, so I would say quite likely." Nyx’s response only made Aria squirm more. It was the first time they met a fangirl in real life.
"We did do a foursome after the cooking stream," Luna reminded the pair with a strong edge to her voice.
"There’s no need to get competitive about everything, bestie."
Before Luna could retort, a new voice spoke up. "You’re here, guys."

Tessa greeted them with a small smile. Their impression of this woman was very positive on a personal level, though her leadership capabilities were questionable at best. However, based on their research into the Nova Circuit guild and its history, Tessa wasn’t the one to blame for their initial downfall. She was just a run-of-the-mill member back when the founders left, leaving this B-tier Arcane Archer to pick up the shattered pieces and do her utmost to keep things going. It was highly doubtful she inherited the properties of the previous guild leaders, though. As such, she was likely forced to pay rent for the HQ as well as anything else owned by those who departed but left some of their properties behind.
"How was your journey here?"
"The minivan you sent to pick us up was a godsend! The driver was professional as well," Aria chirped while returning Tessa’s greeting smile.
"I’m happy to hear that. This was the least I could do for you four. You’re the real godsends, as far as I’m concerned."
As the four ladies continued their chatting, Kaiden couldn’t help but glance sideways. Tessa was waiting for them in the corridor, but behind her, a glass door could be seen.

And in that room, Kaiden saw a face he didn’t expect to ever meet again. Valeria, the woman he confessed to in high school and got rejected by. The same fate awaited David as well when he tried his chance with her.
Upon seeing her image, Kaiden’s features darkened for a brief moment.
Rejecting someone’s confession wasn’t grounds for getting offended or harboring ill will toward a woman—not at all. What solicited such a reaction from him was what she did afterward.

Vaelira always liked to be the center of attention, even if it meant kicking others down to keep the spotlight centered on herself. She spread false rumors about him, such as him being a creepy stalker who drooled incessantly at her mere thought or that he had a visible erection and was stuttering like a clown while confessing. All of these were pure fabrications used to keep their fellow students talking about her.

In the process, she ruined his high school life and even got him in trouble with the teachers. The worst of it all was her two-faced nature; she always liked to act like a kind-hearted girl who was all sunshine and rainbows. This deception of hers was what made Kaiden fall for her in the first place—besides her smoking-hot body, of course.

Vaelira had always been beautiful, but back in high school, she carried a youthful charm: she had a bright, innocent smile that masked her cruel intentions. Now, she had shed that girlish allure for something more refined.

Dressed in a green skirt paired with a fitted top, she no longer had to rely on feigned innocence to turn heads. She carried herself differently, too, with the grace of someone who knew her worth and expected others to acknowledge it.

Yet, despite the change of wardrobe and attitude, Kaiden didn’t believe Vaelira would change on the inside. She looked the part of a sophisticated woman now, but the glint in her eyes still held that same calculating sharpness. The same hunger for attention. The same ability to manipulate others to get what she wanted.
After examining Vaelira for a few seconds through the glass window, Kaiden decided to say hello. It didn’t feel right to just stare at her like a creep.
He pushed the door open and stepped in.

chapters.title: Chapter 130: Promise
paragraphs: The chitter of the many members gathered together quieted all at once. They were in their civilian clothes, but based on their youthful appearances, they must’ve been the group of low-level awakened Kaiden and co were here to help clear the dungeon.
"Kaiden?" Vaelira immediately recognized him. "Is that you?"

"Long time no see," Kaiden replied without a single ounce of joy visible in his features. He wasn’t the kind of person who would pretend to like someone if he didn’t, just so no bad feelings would arise.

"You’ve changed so much!" the blonde woman said with wide eyes and a happy smile. "A big growth spurt did you good, and even with all your clothes, I can tell you’ve been taking care of your body. It’s nice to see you again!"
Vaelira acted as if he was a friend she hadn’t seen in ages and was glad to reunite with, letting Kaiden know she was still the same two-faced bitch he knew her as.
Seeing he wasn’t very fond of meeting her again after the four years of separation since their high school graduation, she elected to keep the conversation going on her own.

"You won’t believe what happened to me! After finishing the graduation ceremony, my parents bought me a Merced*s. As soon as I sat down on its seat, I awakened! I’m an A-tier mage-type, the only one with this high of a tier in the guild. My class is called Arcane Puppetteer."
’Arcane Puppeteer... How fitting of a class for this woman...’ Kaiden thought inwardly with a dry chuckle.

It didn’t take a genius to figure out why she joined a weak guild like Nova Circuit. She could be the queen bee here, always remaining the most important person in the room. In a higher-tiered guild, she would have to contend for attention, but here, it was given to her on a silver platter. Even their guild leader was only B-tier, and Vaelira was of the Arcane subtype to boot, fitting the guild’s theme like a glove. This was the perfect place for her to continue being a nasty woman without suffering any repercussions.
Vaelira then smiled innocently. "What about you? How has life been treating you?"
"I can’t complain; all is fine."
"Isn’t this that guy? I thought Tessa was joking!" a buff man with blonde hair and blue eyes leered.

"What do you mean, Jack?" Vaelira’s question was answered with mocking laughter as multiple other men joined Jack in roaring at Kaiden. The blonde man fought hard to regain control over himself long enough to reply.
"This ’tard is one of those desperate F-tier awakened who shoot porn to make a living."

Hearing this, Vaelira turned her attention back to Kaiden, examining him in search of the truth. A big grin slowly emerged on her lips. She didn’t even try holding it back to keep up appearances. "I see... I’m so sorry to hear that."
"I don’t need your sorry. My life has never been better, I’m as happy as can be."

Replacing her grin, a grimace emerged on her features before she immediately dispatched any such gestures, though her eyes were no longer shining at him in a friendly manner. "... Is that so?" I’m happy for you then."

"But why did Tessa invite an F-tier merc? Surely someone better was available!" a redhead woman grumbled with a great deal of dissatisfaction. She was standing slightly behind Vaelira, signaling her status as her doormat.
"I heard we’re getting four additions, I’m sure the rest will be better."
"From what I know, they’re this dude’s teammates. We contracted a group called Valhalla’s Sinners instead of four individuals."
"Dang, sounds like a heavy metal band."
"... Or a kinky porn studio."

Just as the randoms were beginning to laugh and chat with each other once again, Kaiden clapped his hands together, drawing their attention to him. "Allow me to introduce myself. My name is Kaiden Grey, I’m the leader of the group that’ll be accompanying you on today’s journey. Although we’re at a low level, we strive to become professional combatants, and our attitude reflects that goal of ours. As such, I’ll treat you people with respect, but I expect you to do the same in return. We’ll be fighting together, and our lives might depend on how well we function together."

Kaiden’s gaze swept over the room, and immediately, a palpable shift took place. The once-warm air that brimmed with chatter was reduced to an eerie chill. Some of the weaker awakened shivered, rubbing their hands against their shoulders as if an icy wind had crept through the walls.
The temperature drop wasn’t real. It was the effect resulting from the mere presence the Paragon of Sin had when he was about to utter a threat he meant with all his heart.
His eyes darkened, and the crimson shade of Wrath began bleeding into his irises like liquid fire.
"However," his voice came out low but resonant, cutting through the silence like a blade.
The room stilled, and breaths were held.
"There’s one golden rule I have all of you need to follow if you wish to maintain amicable relations with me. You must not, under any circumstances, mock my teammates."

It felt like his words weren’t just a warning but a decree. For a few seconds, no one moved. Even Vaelira, despite being the type of person who was always on top of her group, was taken aback by the shift in atmosphere. She had recognized Kaiden the moment he stepped into the room, but now, as she stared into his menacing eyes, she found herself questioning if the boy she had mocked in high school had truly become this man.

Then, the silence was interrupted by Jack’s dismissive scoff. With heavy steps, he made his way toward Kaiden, squaring his broad shoulders and cracking his neck like he was gearing up for a fight. His lips twisted into a cocky smirk as he asked, "Or what?"
The temperature plummeted further.
Kaiden’s irises shifted.

Half of each eye turned a burning orange, while the other half became blood red. They didn’t settle into place. No, his eyes began swirling like whirlpools of uncontrollable rage and insatiable hunger. Wrath and Gluttony churned together, dancing in his gaze.
"Or I’ll devour you."
The words were spoken calmly, but they carried the ominous weight of inevitability. Kaiden did not talk metaphorically nor rhetorically—he merely conveyed a simple fact. A promise.
And Jack, for all his previous bravado and being the group’s most prominent tanker, felt a primal shudder crawl up his spine.
"This guy is an F-tier...?" the haughty redhead woman standing behind Vaelira muttered with shaky knees. "No way, right?"

Hearing this, Jack was reminded of the fact that the man standing in front of him was indeed an F-tier nobody. Gathering his bearings, he growled, "You certainly have a way with words, F-tier, but at the end of the day, you’re just one of the wannabes."

The blond man didn’t do his homework. As soon as he read up on Kaiden, he saw he was an F-tier awakened shooting adult videos, so he stopped researching him immediately. As a result, he had no clue that...
"Didn’t he defeat an A-tier?! We should get Jack to back off before..."
"That was at level 1!"
"Yeah, this loser had just awakened. Unlike the noobie Arcane Archmage, we’d been training for years, getting ready to enter the dungeons prepared. Jack would eat this rookie alive."
The chatter of the audience continued until a single, low grunt sounded from Kaiden.
"As you wish."
With that, he got ready to make good on his promise.

It was the effect resulting from the mere presence the Paragon of Sin had when he was about to utter a threat he meant with all his heart.
His eyes darkened, and the crimson shade of Wrath began bleeding into his irises like liquid fire.
"However," his voice came out low but resonant, cutting through the silence like a blade.
The room stilled, and breaths were held.
"There’s one golden rule I have all of you need to follow if you wish to maintain amicable relations with me.
You must not, under any circumstances, mock my teammates."
It felt like his words weren’t just a warning but a decree.
For a few seconds, no one moved.
Even Vaelira, despite being the type of person who was always on top of her group, was taken aback by the shift in atmosphere.

She had recognized Kaiden the moment he stepped into the room, but now, as she stared into his menacing eyes, she found herself questioning if the boy she had mocked in high school had truly become this man.
Then, the silence was interrupted by Jack’s dismissive scoff.
With heavy steps, he made his way toward Kaiden, squaring his broad shoulders and cracking his neck like he was gearing up for a fight.
His lips twisted into a cocky smirk as he asked, "Or what?"
The temperature plummeted further.
Kaiden’s irises shifted.
Half of each eye turned a burning orange, while the other half became blood red.
They didn’t settle into place.
No, his eyes began swirling like whirlpools of uncontrollable rage and insatiable hunger.
Wrath and Gluttony churned together, dancing in his gaze.
"Or I’ll devour you."
The words were spoken calmly, but they carried the ominous weight of inevitability.
Kaiden did not talk metaphorically nor rhetorically—he merely conveyed a simple fact.
A promise.
And Jack, for all his previous bravado and being the group’s most prominent tanker, felt a primal shudder crawl up his spine.
"This guy is an F-tier...?" the haughty redhead woman standing behind Vaelira muttered with shaky knees.
"No way, right?"
Hearing this, Jack was reminded of the fact that the man standing in front of him was indeed an F-tier nobody.
Gathering his bearings, he growled, "You certainly have a way with words, F-tier, but at the end of the day, you’re just one of the wannabes."
The blond man didn’t do his homework.
As soon as he read up on Kaiden, he saw he was an F-tier awakened shooting adult videos, so he stopped researching him immediately.
As a result, he had no clue that...
"Didn’t he defeat an A-tier?!
We should get Jack to back off before..."
"That was at level 1!"
"Yeah, this loser had just awakened.
Unlike the noobie Arcane Archmage, we’d been training for years, getting ready to enter the dungeons prepared.
Jack would eat this rookie alive."
The chatter of the audience continued until a single, low grunt sounded from Kaiden.
"As you wish."
With that, he got ready to make good on his promise.

chapters.title: Chapter 131: Kaiden’s Conviction
paragraphs: Kaiden understood better than anyone just how emotionally vulnerable his girls were. Nyx claimed she no longer cared about the opinions of randoms, but words had power. No matter how strong she acted, being mocked and insulted for their chosen path on repeat would still hurt her. He wasn’t naïve enough to believe otherwise.

He had willingly stepped onto this thorn-covered road, fully aware of the ridicule and scorn it invited. And yes, his Valkyries had chosen to walk beside him; their consent was the final requirement to complete the hidden quest that transformed them into Sinsworn Valkyries—into women who willingly trod the same path as their Paragon of Sin. But just because they had accepted the weight of this path didn’t mean he would stand by and let others spit on their honor.
Kaiden had made a promise to himself.
He would not let others mock them. Not while he still breathed.

His personal pride and his love for these precious, irreplaceable existences would never allow him to look the other way. If anyone thought they could trample on what was his, they would learn the hard way just how wrong they were.
He didn’t care how many times he had to fight.
He didn’t care who stood in his way.
He would never let their dignity be tarnished.

Jack smirked upon seeing his combat-ready stance before mimicking Kaiden’s motions. The blonde brute had trained extensively in hand-to-hand combat, and there was no way he’d lose to some F-tier rookie in an unarmed bout. He cracked his knuckles and grinned from ear to ear. "You’re most certainly S-tier at speech, but let’s see if the force of your bite matches the strength of your barks."
But before either could make a move, a soft thud landed against Kaiden’s back. Warmth spread across his body as delicate hands stroked his chest while a gentle presence pressed into him from behind.

"Calm down, Kai..." Aria whispered lovingly as she rested her head on his back. The tone she used carried a soothing effect in it. She was getting practiced at calming his overly protective boyfriend by this point.
"No need to waste your energy on someone like him," Nyx scoffed dismissively, which was followed up by Luna’s, "That’s right. Ignore the randoms, Kai."

Kaiden exhaled, feeling the tension in his body ease at Aria’s touch and the words of the other two Valkyries. Jack’s smirk faltered, but before he could say anything, a sharp hiss cut through the air.
"Stand down, Jack. Right this instant."

The voice belonged to none other than Tessa. Her eyes burned with anger as she stormed forward. Jack turned his head, and his lips immediately began to part to argue, but the expression on Tessa’s face made him stop.

Tessa took a deep breath before lowering her head in front of Kaiden. "I sincerely apologize for my subordinate’s behavior." There was a trace of exhaustion beneath her voice. "As the leader of this guild, I’ve failed in my responsibilities."
Jack clenched his jaw at the sight, and he wasn’t alone.

"... In the end, nothing happened. One could even argue that I started the tensions. Please raise your head, Guild Leader of Nova Circuit," Kaiden said before turning around so that he could return Aria’s hug.
"You didn’t check the files, did you?" Tessa asked Jack after straightening her spine.
Jack’s silence was all the answer she needed.
Her brow twitched. "The files my assistants sent? The ones instructing everyone to act with respect toward Valhalla’s Sinners?"
Jack finally broke eye contact. Through gritted teeth, he muttered, "Tch. My bad, I guess." The apology was anything but genuine. He turned away, stomping back to his queen bee’s side.
Tessa exhaled while shaking her head. The exhaustion in her eyes was clear now. Dealing with Jack’s ego was draining, and it was the least of her problems as the leader of a crumbling guild.
But then, a wave of murmurs spread through the crowd.
The audience’s gaze followed Kaiden when he turned around toward his girls, and they were met with a sight that left many gasping.

Standing beside him were three breathtakingly beautiful women. Aria, with her supermodel proportions and flowing silver hair. Nyx, whose curvaceous figure and vibrant pink locks gave her an exotic allure that demanded attention from all males and seething jealousy from females. And lastly, Luna, whose lithe yet irresistibly hot frame was decorated by her lush purple hair.
Many stared at the trio with shock, but no one looked more flabbergasted than the queen bee herself.
She had expected Kaiden’s teammates to be three other societal rejects like that nerdy David guy Kaiden had hung around with back in high school.
Instead, not only did the man she had rejected a few years ago have the most insane glow-up she’d ever witnessed, but he was surrounded by three of the most stunning women she had seen.
And worst of all?

They seemed to be devoted to him. None of them gave off an air resembling a gold digger or that of an opportunistic woman who was here to mooch off of a dumb but powerful guy to have an easy ride to a good life.
If that wasn’t enough... ’No, this can’t be...’ she muttered inwardly as a strange feeling assaulted her heart. ’Do I think myself to be uglier than them?!’
For the first time in her life, Vaelira was introduced to the feeling called jealousy.

"The minivans are ready. Change into your combat gear and grab your weapons, alongside any other items you wish to take with you into the dungeon. We’ll move to the site together with your teachers," Tessa instructed the group.

Just as she said so, three adults entered through the same door Kaiden and co did moments before. The newcomers were in their late twenties or early thirties, and their gazes spoke volumes of their experience gained through hard-fought battles in the dungeons. Many injuries riddled their bodies, forcing them into retirement from active duty. As a result, they became instructors guiding the newer generations on their awakened journeys.

Being teachers of the awakened in today’s environment could be best described as bittersweet. On the bright side, they lived to tell the tales of intense life-or-death situations, marking them as survivors when many of their teammates fell. But on the other hand, they could not be healed in full, marking the end of their leveling journey. Once one tasted the sweet taste of power progression, being forced to return to mundane life bore significant mental strain on most.

Now that the tense greetings had concluded, the group moved toward the awaiting minivans. The vehicles were parked in a lot behind the guild’s headquarters. The large, reinforced minivans had been modified into vehicles that could function even in cases of dungeon breaks, featuring sturdy exteriors and spacious interiors to accommodate both people and gear.

Kaiden slid into the backseat of one, flanked by Aria and Luna, while Nyx took the seat in front of them. Next to her sat Tessa and one of the scarred instructions. The other two teachers spread themselves among the remaining vans to keep an eye on the recruits.

The engines roared to life, and the convoy rolled out onto the streets. The drive was long but eventless. The six of them chatted among themselves amicably. Just like Tessa, the teacher did not show signs of mockery toward their chosen path.

chapters.title: Chapter 132: Cleared to Proceed
paragraphs: Kaiden glanced out the window and saw the cityscape slowly fade behind them, replaced by the untamed wilderness. After thirty minutes, the convoy pulled off the road and onto a dirt path leading to a clearing. There, standing tall amid the open landscape, was the dungeon gate.

A perimeter had already been established around it, manned by men dressed in black combat suits. These were employees of the Awakened Association, the governing body responsible for regulating dungeon activity and ensuring that no unauthorized personnel entered restricted zones. They carried high-grade equipment on them to suppress both dungeon threats or rogue awakened if necessary.

One of the guards stepped forward as the minivans came to a stop. He scanned the group without uttering a single word before turning toward Tessa. She knew the procedures, so she walked up to him and handed over the papers that were required for her group to gain entry.

"Your team is clear to proceed," he stated after checking even the minutest details in the papers to ensure everything was in order. He then raised his arm and glanced at his watch. "You have 71 hours to clear the dungeon before we send our forces in."

Even if maximum capacity wasn’t specified by the dungeon gate, only a limited number of people could enter each dimension. The number depended on the dungeon’s rank, which for D-rank was 20, meaning Tessa had organized a full task force for this undertaking.

The only way more people could enter was if someone left or died inside, but there was one additional method: to wait until the final period before the dungeon break began, which in a D-rank dungeon’s case was the last 48 hours. During the final period, the capacity limitations would be doubled, allowing the Awakened Association to send in their own task force even if the original group was still alive inside.
"Understood," Tessa nodded.
With that, the group began unloading their supplies and checking their gear one last time as they prepared to step through the gate into the greatest challenge any of these youths had faced.

Kaiden could take a better look at his team now, and he saw what he’d expected. Most of them were young, not many were older than him. Vaelira was the same age as him at 22, Jack seemed to be around 20. Most of Nova Circuit’s low-level members were around the same age as the blonde musclebrain, with some outliers. A teenage girl caught his eye in particular because her tender features reminded him of Alice, his little sister.

However, unlike his sister, this girl lacked confidence. Her hands were trembling as she checked the contents of her bags one after the other. She was one of the four people in the group who carried multiple large backpacks on their persons without equipping any fancy protective armor or weapons. Instead, they had pickaxes and cooking pans attached to their belts. They were the non-combat units of the group.

Every expedition into uncharted dungeons required mules who did the odd jobs no one else wanted to. This included carrying everyone’s supplies, setting up camp, cooking meals, mining materials, collecting monster drops, etc. Almost all of these people tended to be F-tier awakened. They might as well have been normal citizens based on their power level, but thanks to their status as awakened, they were able to enter dungeons. Non-awakened were not permitted entrance; the dungeon gates simply did not permit them to pass through.
The group gathered around as one of the three instructors, a grizzled man with short-cropped black hair and a jagged scar running across his cheek, spoke up.

"Listen, students. This is your final briefing before stepping through that gate. As you should be well aware, this is a D-rank dungeon with a level limit of 10. That means if you’re level 10 or lower, you can enter freely. If you level up past that point inside, you won’t get kicked out, but you will be unable to return should you leave for one reason or another."

A second instructor continued from here. "The game plan is simple. You will farm levels in the immediate area near the gate first. That way, you can gain a few levels while still having the option to retreat if necessary. Once you’ve strengthened yourselves, you will move deeper into the dungeon."
The instructors’ gazes swept over the group, ensuring everyone was following.

"As for the dungeon itself, it’s a sandy biome with a pyramid theme. Expect mummies, sand felines, scarabs, and other desert-dwelling nasties. These creatures may seem basic but don’t get cocky. D-rank dungeons are no joke."
Some people in the audience straightened their spines with confidence and excitement, while others swallowed with building nervousness.
"The leader of this expedition will be A-tier awakened Vaelira. She will be in charge of all major decisions. Follow her lead, and don’t do anything reckless."
He swept his gaze over the group before locking on Jack.

"Lastly, this will be your first time working alongside mercenaries. Under normal circumstances, we wouldn’t have brought them in, but our hand was forced. Take that as a sign that we don’t believe the sixteen of you alone are enough to clear this dungeon. That means any infighting is straight-up unacceptable. Like it or not, you need the four of them to make it back alive and successful. Get that through your thick heads. Understood?"

Many nodded at his words. While most still viewed the mercenaries with skepticism, if not outright condescension, no one could deny the threat posed by a D-rank dungeon, especially now that their seniors wouldn’t be by their sides. In the end, survival took precedence over pride. If these outsiders made their odds of returning better in one piece, then so be it.

"Guild members," Tessa spoke up. "You’ve spent years preparing for this exact moment. Remember the teachings your instructors left you with, trust your allies, and do your best. If you can do all three of these, you’ll return safe and sound. You’ll gain recognition from your fellow awakened, furthermore, you’ll gain levels, riches, and invaluable experience. That’s all from your leader. Make me, your teachers, and the legacy of Nova Circuit proud!"
"Yes, Leader!" a chorus of cries replied.

chapters.title: Chapter 133: Into the Desert Dungeon!
paragraphs: "Welcome back, everyone," Kaiden said, greeting his viewers. Nyx posted the announcement of the upcoming dungeon descent on their socials yesterday as soon as the decision was made to accept Tessa’s invitation. The posts on the internet and the awakened platform received a lot of favorable reactions, their followers were excited to witness this event.
- Lady Leia: Heh. I’m first. Suck it, dumb bitches.
- Kaiden’s Wife: Curses! I must train my reflexes, I was slow once again!
Princeless Princess timed out Lady Leia for thirty minutes. Reason: Usage of profanities.
- Princeless Princess: Hi Kaiden! I wish you good luck on this dangerous undertaking!
- Shadow Warrior: Dang son, already in a D-rank dungeon?!
- Thirsty247: My senior is rapidly moving up in the world of awakened.
- TouchGrass: He didn’t accept you as his junior. He didn’t even acknowledge your request to be taught.
- Thirsty247: Princess, can you ban this fatass? I bet he’s a drooler irl.
- Feet Sniffer: I did a little bit of research, and it turns out this is not just a D-rank dungeon, but an uncharted one at that.

"Indeed, Feet Sniffer is right. We were hired by the Nova Circuit guild as mercs to help clear this dungeon. It had the annoying restriction of allowing entrance only to those who were level 10 or below," Kaiden revealed, making the chat buzz. People were rapidly flooding in; nearly a thousand viewers were tuning in to the stream already.
"Ha?" Multiple gasps rang through the gathered awakened. They were about to step through the gate into the dungeon, but then Kaiden started talking loudly to a ’Feet Sniffer,’ confusing them greatly.
"Did he lose his marbles?"
"I-I-I think he’s streaming right now..." the timid teenage girl with many backpacks muttered shyly.
"Now that you mention, he did indeed upload first-person videos from what I remember, but I thought he had a recording device... How does he record?"

While many curiously observed Kaiden, a robotic humming sounded as Vaelira activated her mana camera, intending to stream as well. Normally, she should’ve had very little following as a trainee who just started her dungeon-diving career not long ago, but she smartly used the opportunity to begin a Yout*be career as soon as she awakened, where she vlogged her daily life.

Even though Vaelira remained level 1 for multiple years due to the schooling she received at Nova Circuit, people were still fascinated with her because of her A-tier status. It was a real privilege to follow the journey of an awakened with her illustrious tier from before she even killed her first monster.
Naturally, her social persona and hot body also played a major role in her success as a vlogger. A pretty face went a long way to make people click on video thumbnails.
"Welcome back to the Vaelira Show, everyone!"

Thanks to her four years of content creation and the money her parents spent on advertising this dungeon descent of hers, Vaelira’s stream had more than ten times the number of viewers compared to Valhalla’s Sinners.

With that, it was time to go. One after the other, the members of the expedition stepped through the dungeon gate. The moment they did so, the world around them shifted. The cool morning air was replaced by the searing heat of a sunlit wasteland. The scent of the green clearing where the dungeon gate emerged on Earth was replaced by dry, sandy winds.
Golden desert dunes stretched endlessly as far as the eye could see; there was nothing but sand... Sand on top of sand. With one exception. In the far distance stood a pyramid.

As the only positive note of this dungeon’s environment, a lush oasis surrounded the gate and its immediate proximity, offering a contrast that was akin to heaven and earth when compared to the barren expanse that lay beyond. Palm trees and other greenery surrounded a crystal-clear pond in the center, it was a body of water that was teeming with fish.

A small camp had already been established under Tessa’s direction. Several tents had been erected, and supply crates rested in the shade, containing water, rations, and dungeon survival gear. The scouts she assigned had already surveyed the surrounding kilometer for immediate dangers.

Who were these scouts? Usually rangers and rogues, people who were good at being sneaky. Being a scout was the most dangerous role an awakened could have, even triumphing that of the tanker, the people who took hits on purpose so that their teammates wouldn’t have to. The reason for such danger could be accredited to the many threats looming in a dungeon that no man had ever set foot in.

Not every dungeon had a safe starting area; sometimes, monsters were observed camping the dungeon gates, especially if it was an older dungeon and the monsters had learned that humans might step through the entrance at any moment. If that wasn’t enough, the environment of the dungeon also posed grave threats to the scouts.

There were reports of scouts stepping into a dungeon gate, and instead of landing on solid ground, a cold ocean awaited them, and as luck would have it, a Leviathan monster just so happened to pass by, eating them all in an instant.
All that is to say, scouting was a dangerous job, but it paid handsomely. Only a few class archetypes, such as the healers or truly outstanding damage dealers, could command higher pay than them.

Vaelira clapped her hands to gather attention. "This oasis will serve as our base of operations for the first day. We’ll spend the next twenty-four hours grinding experience so that we can tackle the later monsters, gathering information on enemy patterns and acclimating our bodies to the desert biome. Tomorrow, we begin the march toward the pyramid. For now, you have ten minutes to take your indicated tents, secure your belongings, and get ready to move out."

None opposed her suggested plan. Taking time to adjust and level up was their best bet, and everyone understood it. Rushing through an unknown desert was a fool’s errand. As such, the group dispersed. Since Kaiden and the squad had no clue which tent was theirs, they remained in place, waiting to see which one was free. However, before that could become clear, Vaelira approached the four of them once the others had left.

"This is Kaiden, one of the many boys who confessed to me in high school..." she revealed slyly to her mana camera. Then, having read a question from her chatters, she grimaced visibly with disgust. "Did I go out with him? Gods, no!"
"What the hell is going on? What’s this blonde bitch on about?" Luna growled, not liking the attitude of Vaelira one bit.

Not bothered by Vaelira’s taunts, Kaiden replied in a neutral tone. "Long story short, I was deceived by her kind persona act, so I tried my chance with her. I was shot down, and then she fabricated lies to mock me for whatever reason."

"Kind persona? You’re telling me this chick’s hot piece of ass played no role in your confession whatsoever?" Nyx asked with a coy smile, instantly understanding the main reason why the inexperienced Kaiden crushed on her.

chapters.title: Chapter 134: Pack Rat
paragraphs: "You can’t blame teenage boys and their rampaging hormones... They all make mistakes. I would know; Damian can be a real challenge sometimes. I once got a call from the principal saying he confessed to his English teacher Miss Andrea," Aria added in defense of her boyfriend, though her words did not manage to make Kaiden feel better one bit.
While Kaiden might’ve not appreciated the words of his Space and Moon Valkyries, he just chuckled amusedly.

Vaelira, on the other hand, had a much stronger reaction. She squinted her eyes with hostility as she studied the two women. "Did you, pink hair, just call your expedition leader a chick with a hot piece of ass, and did you, silver hair, imply that confessing to me was a mistake? I must’ve heard wrong; explain yourselves."
It was Kaiden who spoke up before either of his Valkyries could.

"You heard them just right. You’re a sexy woman, and confessing to you was a big mistake of mine. I was all respectful and proper while doing so, you even got a rose bouquet from me. Not wanting to buy flowers for the girl I liked with pocket money I got from my parents, I worked an afternoon as a dishwasher in a restaurant to gather the funds. Yet you felt it was right to ruin my high school social life in return by spouting nonsensical lies. I could only chat with rejects like David, thanks to you. So, tell me, expedition leader, how exactly were either of my partners wrong in their statements?"

Vaelira was taken aback, not expecting such strong words from Kaiden. Back in high school, he protested against the lies for a bit, but after a while, he just accepted them for what they were. This combative version of Kaiden was not something she was used to.

She checked the reaction of her chat, and her heart skipped a beat when only ~75% of the chatters were mockingly laughing at Kaiden as a dude who got cruelly rejected after confessing. The remaining 25% was women sending blushing emojis and men spamming wide-eyed emojis regarding the three girls.

- HateWomen: I just found a new female specimen to observe after getting betrayed by Supreme Empress Luna, yet here he is again to haunt me... When will these nightmares end? If he charms Queen Vaelira as well, I’ll find him in real life...
- BubblyPink: You know them? Do they have a social?
- BraveHero69: Tell us!

Not wishing to promote Kaiden’s group, Vaelira quickly muted the user called HateWomen. There was no notification of it sent to the chat; moderating could be done without messages likeVaelira permanently muted HateWomenbeing public.

"Is there a problem, Vael?" Sasha, the redhead woman who stood behind her during introductions, asked while walking toward the group. She was flanked by the towering Jack, who now sported heavy armor and a giant mace and shield, and a black-haired guy with a knight’s armor and longsword called Leon. Together with Vaelira, these four were the main force of the Nova Circuit expedition group.
Vaelira stared into Kaiden’s gaze for a few seconds before shaking her head. "I was just introducing the mercs to the viewers. Isn’t that right, Kaiden?"
He nodded. "We’re here to level up and earn riches, not to settle some petty high school drama that happened years ago."
"Good."
With that, the blonde woman turned on her heels and walked away, followed by her lackeys.
"Well, that’s a great start. We entered the dungeon a minute ago, and there’s already brewing inner conflicts..." Nyx mused.
"At least it’ll be a good viewing experience."
None of the ladies felt like addressing Kaiden’s statement.
They soon found their tent. It wasn’t one of those cramped, single-person shelters only good for lying down. Instead, it was a proper expedition tent, spacious enough to stand and move around in.

Four beds lined its walls, each with a mattress and a set of neatly folded blankets. In the center, a wooden table with four chairs provided a place to eat, strategize, or simply rest between fights. The tent’s walls were reinforced to withstand the desert winds, and a small ventilation opening near the top ensured fresh air circulation.
"Umm... Excuse me..." A timid voice sounded from outside the tent.
"Come in!" Aria replied cheerily. They knew it was the young girl with many backpacks from her voice alone.
"T-thank you..." she said while stepping in. "Umm... I’ve been assigned as your pack mule."

Such a phrase for her profession didn’t sit well with Kaiden when it was her lips that uttered it. Pack mule was the common term used to describe her job, but it was not the official one, just like how the term ’commoners’ was the unofficial but popular way to describe non-awakened people. "What’s your name?"
"Packrat."
The fact that this time around, she didn’t even hesitate nor stutter with her response made all four observers flinch. "What Kaiden asked for is the name given to you by your parents," Luna informed.
"Oh. S-sorry... Elara."
It wasn’t difficult for the four to understand what was going on. She was ridiculed by the others so much that she accepted such a name as her real one.
"You’re going to be our dungeon aide?" Aria asked with a tender tone, using the official term for Elara’s profession.
The timid girl nodded, "Y-yes... Four teams of four were made so that combatants could hunt monsters effectively, and each team was assigned a pack mule."

"Alright. We’re happy to have you, Elara," Kaiden decreed with a smile. He didn’t expect Vaelira to split the team up, but if he thought about it, it made sense. Hunting XP as a group of 20 would be ineffective. It was best to make smaller teams and then rejoin each other once the 24 hours of XP grinding had been concluded and it was time to begin the clear in full.

Elara, who had brown hair and a few freckles that adorned her innocent-looking face, showed signs of surprise. She expected them to go with the Packrat name and treat her as a simple mule, not like this. "T-thank you..." she muttered with confusion, then asked, "Can I help with the preparation?"

"Thank you, but we’re ready to go as is," Nyx replied while checking her dagger. With that, the five left the tent and saw two groups walking in the distance. They’d already left the camp in search of monsters to slay.

The final team—consisting of Vaelira, Sasha, Jack, and Leon—sat around a table, playing a board game while drinking and lavishly feasting on provisions. When Kaiden and his squad emerged from the tent, Sasha was the one to address them.

"We’ll be rotating shifts for hunting and guarding. Each team will hunt for six hours and take a two-hour turn defending the camp. We’ll keep this schedule for the next sixteen hours, which means you’ll get four hours of rest and twelve hours of hunting time. We volunteered to take the first guard shift, and the other two teams will cover the next four hours after us. That means you guys will start your guard duty in six hours."
"Okay."

It was obvious what was going on. Vaelira’s team remained behind first so the other three teams would act as test dummies for them. After the first 2 hours were up, they would know if there was anything dangerous they should look out for during their hunt.

Furthermore, by making Kaiden and co have their guard session last, their hunting would be inefficient because hunting for six hours straight was not feasible with their current Endurance stat under the scorching heat.

Nevertheless, Kaiden didn’t offer any rebuttals. As a merc, it wasn’t his place to do so. Being given harsher conditions than guild members was par for the course, though he would make sure to remember how they were treated by Nova Circuit. Any sensible guild would treat mercs with respect should they wish to retain working relations in case another difficult dungeon propped up.
"Let’s go."
And just like that, Valhalla’s Sinners and their aide set out on a hunt across the desert.
