chapters.title: Chapter 135: Desert Monsters
paragraphs: "Are we in a sauna? We must be in a sauna..." Luna grumbled while airing her armor out to the best of her abilities. Gamer girls were not meant to endure the scorching desert heat.
"At least you’re wearing light armor... I’m gonna die," Nyx decreed in a matter of factly tone. She and Kaiden were the only ones in medium armor.

"Come on, girls, it’s not that bad..." Aria said cheerily, attempting to help the mood. Instead of achieving her goal, she only succeeded in eliciting two heads snapping in her direction. Nyx and Luna scoffed in sync when they saw the comfy mage robes that adorned her body.
"Hypocrite Princess..." they cursed under their breaths in perfect unison.

"Would you like some water?" Elara asked as she reached into one of the four bags strapped to her. The largest bag, which was nearly as tall as she was, hung on her back. The second was slung across her stomach, while the final two rested on her sides.
The two girls gratefully accepted the bottles of water and gulped them down eagerly. After finishing, they poured what little water was left over their heads to cool off.

Thankfully, they didn’t need to be sparing with water because not only did the guild have magically cooled containers full of water at the camp, but the oasis acted as a freshwater source as well. Lack of water would only be troublesome once they left the oasis behind as they could only bring what they could carry on them, forced to leave the large coolers behind.
"You’re really strong, Elara. What’s your Strength stat?"
Kaiden’s question met with her usual adorable "Umm..." sound before she gathered her bearings to reply properly. "24."
"Hoh? I’m surprised. No wonder you carry those big bags so easily."
Before she could address his words, it was Nyx who spoke up. "Are you from that company? What was their name again? Titanforge?"
"Yes," she nodded.
"What’s that?" Aria, who wasn’t overly educated in the world of the awakened as she was busy with her non-awakened duties before meeting Kaiden, asked.

The knowledgeable, pink-haired beauty was happy to offer her information. "Titanforge is a company that trains F-tier awakened, or those who don’t wish to be combatants but still want to participate in dungeon clearings. Their trainees receive help from stronger combatants to reach level 5, and they invest all gained points into the Strength stat. Furthermore, they receive proper education in dungeon matters that a person in a support role like theirs should be aware of, such as which ores to mine. Lastly, they also receive physical training to increase their natural Strength and Endurance stats, allowing them to carry incredible weights for long distances and mine with eye-popping speed and efficiency."
"And once a trainee finishes their training?"

"Before being accepted into Titanforge as a trainee, you must sign a contract with them. Once the training has concluded, guilds can purchase their contracts for 10 Chronos, which will bind the dungeon aide to work for the customer guild for the next decade. Furthermore, 30% of their salary in that time duration goes to Titanforge."
"What the hell?!" Luna shouted with outrage. Kaiden and Aria were also shocked. If Elara wasn’t present, they would’ve called this practice straight-up slavery.

"Yeah, I know..." Nyx said with a sad sigh. "The government doesn’t know what to do. People want to work as dungeon aides because the pay is better than what most of them could earn in the world of non-awakened, but most guilds don’t want to hire nor train dungeon aides, thinking it to be a waste of time. Furthermore, guilds don’t want to employ level 1 awakened to act as aides due to the dungeons’ capacity limit. If Elara and the other three aides weren’t as capable as they are, we would’ve needed like twelve people to do their work, meaning only eight combatants could enter alongside the group of aides.

To smaller guilds, paying 10 Chronos and then a salary of something in the range of $3,000 a month is much more worthwhile than training their own aides from scratch. The biggest guilds do have the resources to train their aides, but they’re often E or even higher-tier awakened who can double in as combatants should the need arise. Anyways, long story short: the government right now is turning a blind eye to this practice. They don’t endorse it, but no penalties have been given to companies like Titanforge nor the guilds who employ the aides."

Throughout Nyx’s explanation, Elara’s expression turned more dejected by the second. Kaiden and co felt troubled about it all. It was a moral gray area. Elara looked to be around 16 years old. If she was ready to dive into dungeons with only a pickaxe at her side, then life must’ve been truly trying for her.

A salary of $3,000, or more accurately the ~$2,100 that would remain after Titanforge’s cut, could be their best opportunity to provide for themselves and their loved ones, especially considering most guilds offered free accommodation and meals for their members in their buildings.
It was easy to call Titanforge the big bad, and they were most certainly horrible, exploitative sons of bitches, but they also presented opportunities to people in need.
"HHRRAAAGGHHH...!" A dry, guttural roar sounded all of a sudden, bringing them out of their stupor.
<Desert Mummy - Level 8>
<Desert Mummy - Level 7>
<Desert Mummy - Level 9>
<Desert Mummy - Level 8>

"Desert mummies, watch out!" Elara shouted, shifting into professional mode instantly. Unlike Kaiden and his Valkyries, who enjoyed the assistance of the system, this teenage girl wasn’t shown details such as the monsters’ type or levels, but thanks to her training and preparation for this dungeon dive in particular, she was knowledgeable.

"They have multiple annoying abilities: [Burial Instinct] lets them sink into the sand to evade attacks and ambush targets. They have a debuff called [Thirst of the Dead], making our bodies dry up rapidly when they’re in our close proximity. [Dried Flesh Resilience] lets them shrug off slashing and piercing damage. Blunt or magic attacks are the best to kill them. Lastly-"
"Hhrrraaahhhkkk-sssshhhhhkkk!"
Before the brown-haired girl could finish her detailing, the mummies let off a loud, wailing sound.

The sand around them stirred before splitting open. From the depths beneath, a swarm of about 50 large scarabs poured forth. These monsters were much bigger than their insect counterparts that could be found on Earth, growing as large as small-sized dog breeds.
Some clung to the mummies’ ragged bandages, crawling over their decayed bodies like loyal parasites ready to defend their hosts, while others moved toward Kaiden’s group.
<Necrocarab - level 4>
<Necrocarab - level 5>
<Necrocarab - level 3>

Elara let out a nervous sigh as she finished, "And lastly... [Scavenger’s Call] lets them summon necrocarabs, their loyal pawns." Having said her piece, the dungeon aide knew it wasn’t her time to shine. She would only get in the way if she stayed. Using her high Strength stat, she leaped back, getting out of the combatants’ way.

Although they were also informed of this monster’s specialties after accepting Tessa’s request, they didn’t have much time to prepare and memorize such details. The trusty knowledge of their aide came in handy.

"This is certainly a big step up from the F-rank dungeon... Our first encounter already put us in a bit of a bind," Kaiden chuckled dryly. But then, he turned serious. Gripping his war axe with both hands, he decreed, "Let’s do this, ladies. Mode: Wrath."
Just as the Paragon of Sin entered his aggressive combat stance, his Sinsworn Valkyries called forth their signature abilities as well.
"[Stormblade]," Luna intoned, materializing a crackling blade of storm energies in her hands.
"[Telekinesis]," Nyx said, grabbing her dagger from its sheath and aiming it at the necrocarabs.

"[Lunar Arc]!" Aria shouted, hitting one of the charging insect monsters right in the face, greatly damaging it. However, it was not a one-hit kill; its sturdy exoskeleton protected it from death. Thanks to the arc of the projectile, it hit multiple others on their side.
The Moon Valkyrie followed her initial spell up with [Crescent Volley]. The many small projectiles assaulted the injured scarabs, many gave up the fight after resisting a few shots.

Nyx wasted no time in seizing the opportunity her friend had created. She raised her hands, pulling the fallen scarabs’ corpses toward her before activating [Kinetic Shard]. Their shattered remains broke apart into dozens of sharp fragments. With a push of her arms, she sent them hurtling forward, turning the dead into weapons against the living. The air filled with sounds of crunches as the shards pierced through the incoming necrocarabs, their own hardened shells were used against them.

Even still, a dozen or so scarabs managed to reach them. At least, they would’ve, but... "We can’t have the pair of Miss Fragiles take a hit, they’ll crumble from a little scratch... Right, Kai?" Luna purred with a smirk, shooting Aria and Nyx a side-eyed glance before creating a gust of wind with [Aero Repulsion] that blasted through the battlefield, sending the charging scarabs tumbling back to their masters.
"Be a good girl, Luna... You can have your catfight once we get back to the camp."

Kaiden’s words earned him a strong scoff from his Storm Valkyrie, who didn’t appreciate his word usage, but they both quickly turned serious, fully aware that what they were doing required their utmost focus, or they could lose everything due to a mere moment’s carelessness.

sentences.text: "Are we in a sauna?
We must be in a sauna..." Luna grumbled while airing her armor out to the best of her abilities.
Gamer girls were not meant to endure the scorching desert heat.
"At least you’re wearing light armor...
I’m gonna die," Nyx decreed in a matter of factly tone.
She and Kaiden were the only ones in medium armor.
"Come on, girls, it’s not that bad..." Aria said cheerily, attempting to help the mood.
Instead of achieving her goal, she only succeeded in eliciting two heads snapping in her direction.
Nyx and Luna scoffed in sync when they saw the comfy mage robes that adorned her body.
"Hypocrite Princess..." they cursed under their breaths in perfect unison.
"Would you like some water?" Elara asked as she reached into one of the four bags strapped to her.
The largest bag, which was nearly as tall as she was, hung on her back.
The second was slung across her stomach, while the final two rested on her sides.
The two girls gratefully accepted the bottles of water and gulped them down eagerly.
After finishing, they poured what little water was left over their heads to cool off.
Thankfully, they didn’t need to be sparing with water because not only did the guild have magically cooled containers full of water at the camp, but the oasis acted as a freshwater source as well.
Lack of water would only be troublesome once they left the oasis behind as they could only bring what they could carry on them, forced to leave the large coolers behind.
"You’re really strong, Elara.
What’s your Strength stat?"
Kaiden’s question met with her usual adorable "Umm..." sound before she gathered her bearings to reply properly.
"Hoh?
I’m surprised.
No wonder you carry those big bags so easily."
Before she could address his words, it was Nyx who spoke up.
"Are you from that company?
What was their name again?
Titanforge?"
"Yes," she nodded.
"What’s that?" Aria, who wasn’t overly educated in the world of the awakened as she was busy with her non-awakened duties before meeting Kaiden, asked.
The knowledgeable, pink-haired beauty was happy to offer her information.
"Titanforge is a company that trains F-tier awakened, or those who don’t wish to be combatants but still want to participate in dungeon clearings.
Their trainees receive help from stronger combatants to reach level 5, and they invest all gained points into the Strength stat.
Furthermore, they receive proper education in dungeon matters that a person in a support role like theirs should be aware of, such as which ores to mine.

Lastly, they also receive physical training to increase their natural Strength and Endurance stats, allowing them to carry incredible weights for long distances and mine with eye-popping speed and efficiency."
"And once a trainee finishes their training?"
"Before being accepted into Titanforge as a trainee, you must sign a contract with them.
Once the training has concluded, guilds can purchase their contracts for 10 Chronos, which will bind the dungeon aide to work for the customer guild for the next decade.
Furthermore, 30% of their salary in that time duration goes to Titanforge."
"What the hell?!" Luna shouted with outrage.
Kaiden and Aria were also shocked.
If Elara wasn’t present, they would’ve called this practice straight-up slavery.
"Yeah, I know..." Nyx said with a sad sigh.
"The government doesn’t know what to do.

People want to work as dungeon aides because the pay is better than what most of them could earn in the world of non-awakened, but most guilds don’t want to hire nor train dungeon aides, thinking it to be a waste of time.
Furthermore, guilds don’t want to employ level 1 awakened to act as aides due to the dungeons’ capacity limit.
If Elara and the other three aides weren’t as capable as they are, we would’ve needed like twelve people to do their work, meaning only eight combatants could enter alongside the group of aides.
To smaller guilds, paying 10 Chronos and then a salary of something in the range of $3,000 a month is much more worthwhile than training their own aides from scratch.
The biggest guilds do have the resources to train their aides, but they’re often E or even higher-tier awakened who can double in as combatants should the need arise.
Anyways, long story short: the government right now is turning a blind eye to this practice.
They don’t endorse it, but no penalties have been given to companies like Titanforge nor the guilds who employ the aides."
Throughout Nyx’s explanation, Elara’s expression turned more dejected by the second.
Kaiden and co felt troubled about it all.
It was a moral gray area.
Elara looked to be around 16 years old.
If she was ready to dive into dungeons with only a pickaxe at her side, then life must’ve been truly trying for her.

A salary of $3,000, or more accurately the ~$2,100 that would remain after Titanforge’s cut, could be their best opportunity to provide for themselves and their loved ones, especially considering most guilds offered free accommodation and meals for their members in their buildings.
It was easy to call Titanforge the big bad, and they were most certainly horrible, exploitative sons of bitches, but they also presented opportunities to people in need.
"HHRRAAAGGHHH...!" A dry, guttural roar sounded all of a sudden, bringing them out of their stupor.

chapters.title: Chapter 136: Battle Against the Mummies
paragraphs: The momentary clearance in the swarm, thanks to the onslaught of the ladies, created an opening, an opportunity that Kaiden seized immediately.
"[Warpath]!" Kaiden roared, refusing to disclose he had [Silent Casting]. He planned to hide that ability as his secret weapon meant to only be brought out during times of ultimate need.

His firm muscles tensed as he sprinted forward, fearlessly charging into the group of monsters. Kaiden was fully aware that frontline duties would fall on him, and he was more than happy with said role.
How couldn’t he? Not only did he get to shield his Valkyries from harm, but besides his sole fire spell, he was useless from range.

The magically enhanced dash sent him barreling toward the nearest desert mummy. The monster lifted an arm to intercept his raised war axe’s arc, but the sheer momentum behind Kaiden’s charge made the motion one second too late.
*Crack!*

Listening to Elara’s words of advice, he used the blunt end of his axe to slam into its ribs with a bone-shattering impact. The creature staggered backward as its dried, leathery body absorbed the blow better than any human with the same Vitality stat could, but Kaiden followed up with a second swing. Its force made the mummy shriek with pain while getting tossed high into the skies.
Once finishing its airborne journey, the monster landed with a loud thud, the impact of which was the final drop needed.
[You’ve slain Desert Mummy (Level 8). You’ve gained 1240 XP.]
A red essence orb materialized on top of its body, and [Harvest], his Gluttony spell that was always active, brought the orb in automatically as if it had a gravitational pull of its own.
{Vitality: 23 +0.1%}

Kaiden grimaced at the sight. It was the first time he saw the buff... he hoped it would be a bit stronger.’A red orb gave me Vitality, and only a minor buff at that. [Harvest] will only be really useful if I enter battle with a giant monster horde.’
Luna was stalking right behind Kaiden, acting perfectly in line with her role as the speedy damage dealer of the group who would look for the ideal opportunity to make her move.

Her [Stormblade] crackled with raw power as she jumped and then slashed at another mummy, following up instantly with [Thunder Slash]. A shockwave of electricity tore through the air, striking the target square in the chest, alongside a few scarabs that were attached to its body like living armor.

Despite Kaiden and Luna charging into the fray, the monsters didn’t sit idly by. They made their move by sending a group of scarabs to swarm the backline. There was only so much Kaiden and Luna could do to protect them from the onslaught of such a high number of enemies.
However, Kaiden didn’t need to fear. As his beautiful Moon Valkyrie had informed him yesterday, they were not mere props to make him look good and have fun with during times of peace.
They wished to become proper warrior women, and they were equipped with the proper tools to achieve said wish.
Aria raised her hands, aiming her pointer finger at the front of the swarm. "[Lunar Arc]! [Crescent Volley]!"

A rapid barrage of crescent-shaped projectiles pelted the incoming insects, exploding on impact. The single large blast was followed by numerous small ones that shredded through their ranks, reducing many of the creatures to twitching husks. But some were still ready to fight, and they were closing in.

Nyx extended her hand as she focused all her mental prowess on her next move. Her beautiful eyes glowed with power as she activated [Telekinesis], attempting to seize a cluster of incoming necrocarabs. She gritted her teeth, straining to lift them, but the stubborn insects barely budged. A frustrated sigh escaped her lips. Even with all her investments into the Magic stat, her ability to influence living creatures was still lacking.
"Fine. Plan B."

She invoked [Astral Summon: Earth], this time forgoing her favored daggers. Instead, two solid spheres of hardened stone materialized in her palms, which she hurled at the oncoming swarm. The heavy projectiles slammed into the necrocarabs, and her choice of element—as well as weapon type—was paying dividends when their thick exoskeletons cracked under the sheer blunt force, sending chitin and ichor splattering across the sandstone floor.

Back on the frontlines, another Desert Mummy snarled and lunged at Kaiden with its withered claws. He barely managed to twist his body out of the way, and its [Thirst of the Dead] aura was rearing its ugly head: he could already feel his throat drying up thanks to the debuff. "Fighting these mummies in melee range for extended periods of time is just asking to be sucked dry—and not in the manner I enjoy..."

He grumbled, receiving many eye-rolls, both from his girls and the ladies in the audience who were watching the ongoing battle with rapidly beating hearts and eyes that couldn’t be peeled from the stream.
"[Fiery Burst]!"

A wave of fire erupted from his hand, engulfing the mummy in flames. Its ancient bandages caught fire instantly, and soon, the blaze spread over its entire body. The undead thrashed and wailed, but Kaiden wasn’t about to let it recover.

Raising his weapon high, he activated [Doom Strike], channeling power into his next attack. With a mighty downward swing, he brought his axe crashing into the mummy’s skull, shattering its head completely and ending its existence.
[You’ve slain Desert Mummy (Level 7). You’ve gained 1080 XP.]

After a minute of back and forth, the battle was at long last winding down. There were no more mummies left to slay; only a few of their summoned minions remained. They didn’t dematerialize after the demise of their masters, becoming independent entities instead.
Kaiden switched stances, transitioning to Gluttony Mode.
He stepped toward one of the remaining necrocarabs and swung the blunt end of his war axe down on it, crushing the creature’s hardened exoskeleton with a crack.
Now that its natural armor was shattered, he reached down, lifting its twitching body in his free hand. His grin widened.
"Thanks for the meal. [Ravenous Bite]."

His fangs extended, sinking into the exposed flesh beneath the broken shell. Mana and vitality drained from the struggling creature, fueling him. The scarab’s twitching movements slowed before ceasing altogether.
Once the Valkyries dispatched the remaining scarabs, they gathered around their man before eyeing him with deadpan expressions.
"No kissing until you get your hands on a toothbrush," Luna declared.

"I-I mean..." Aria tried to find the appetite required to be the good girlfriend who was ready to embrace her man’s wild side, but her stomach churned loudly in strong protest. "Yeah, no, I can’t. Sorry, Kai..."
"Kekeke. At least you tried. That’s what matters."
Hearing Nyx’s words, three pairs of eyes found themselves examining her curiously, wondering if she was down for some freaky action. The Space Valkyrie strongly shook her head. "Nope."

Kaiden wiped the scarab’s blood from his lips, letting a fulfilled sigh escape his lungs. This recovery ability was amazing, and despite how unappetizing the prospect of draining the blood of monsters appeared beforehand, once he unlocked the ability, it strangely no longer felt like that. It was just him making use of his spells, nothing more, nothing less.

"I gotta say, we’re stronger than I expected," Kaiden decreed proudly, not bothered by the evident distaste his girls had for his lips smeared with scarab blood. He didn’t come to this dungeon to make out with them but to farm levels.

That was exactly what they did for the next few hours, successfully reaching level 10 after triumphing in lots of dangerous encounters. Besides the mummies and their scarab allies, the monsters they encountered were felines with black furs called khopesh jackals, who used speed and pack tactics to ambush their prey.

The other type of monster that appeared was a large scorpion called doomstinger. Unlike the mummies with their slow-drying debuff, a single sting from this monster would instantly turn the liquid in the body into poison, granted that the recipient didn’t have high enough Vitality stat to resist or potions/abilities with a similar effect.
Vitality was an almighty stat that granted general resistance against all harmful effects, be they poison, damage from a weapon, fall from heights, etc.
"Heeelp!"
"Rebecca!"
"Sister! Noo!!"
Loud shouts sounded from a short distance all of a sudden, alerting the group.

chapters.title: Chapter 137: Dune Maw Ambush
paragraphs: Kaiden and his Valkyries snapped their heads toward the source of the cries and swiftly rushed to the scene.
What they saw was grim.

A massive, worm-like creature had emerged from beneath the dunes. Currently, it was busy feasting on its prey. The woman—Rebecca, if her teammates’ cries were any indication—lay in the sand, with her entire lower body gone, devoured. She was rapidly bleeding out onto the golden grains beneath her. Her breaths were shallow, her eyes wide with terror as if she struggled to accept that what had just happened to her was reality and not a horrible nightmare.

Her teammates were doing their best to save her; they struck at the monster’s hide repeatedly, but their attacks barely left a scratch. The creature’s exterior was resisting everything they threw at it.
<Dune Maw - Level 13>
Kaiden gritted his teeth at the sight. "Damn it. Is this that phenomenon you mentioned, Nyx?"
Yes..." the Space Valkyrie nodded her head with a grim expression, observing the poor woman whose fate was all but sealed.

Elara spoke up with a trembling tone, explaining what the pair was talking about. Based on her ashen face and trembling voice, she did more so to herself out of pure shock than to inform her teammates. "The rank of a dungeon is indicative of its clear difficulty. Stronger ones can enter areas meant for weaker beings, and this phenomenon occurs more often the higher the dungeon’s rank is."
Five ashen expressions watched the ongoings, momentarily frozen with the realization that it could’ve been one of them in Rebecca’s place. But then... "We have to help!" Aria cried with alarm.
Luna felt the same, evidenced by the materialization of her [Stormblade].

Elara wasn’t informative this time around. She grimaced, "I don’t know what kind of a worm it is... The scout reports only included the three entry-level monsters—the desert mummies, khopesh jackals, and doomstingers... I’ve never seen this one, not even in my extensive study preparation.

"Burrowing beneath the sand to reposition and having a sturdy hide is definitely a given," Nyx said her thoughts out loud, but then only silence followed. They had no clue what else to expect from its arsenal. To make it even worse, not only was this a level 13 monster, but a physically imposing one at that. It must’ve weighed tens of tons and reached 15 meters (50 feet) in length.

This meant that comparing it to monsters that hunted in groups would not do its might justice. It was akin to comparing the Silverback Mauler that almost killed them to a rat monster that Kaiden easily swatted away. Just thanks to its physical proportions, it had supreme strength that came from having to move this giant mass around. The mass itself then improved its Vitality, making it a real frightening opponent.

Kaiden gritted his teeth. He wasn’t one to care about heroism, but losing a quarter of their fighters even before leaving the starting area would mark this undertaking a failure. They would likely be forced to retreat. "Let’s help them. Remain behind me, only strike opportunistically. Keep your distance at all costs."
The ladies nodded at his statement with determined expressions.
Taking up formation, they began moving toward the massacre happening in the distance.

Behind him, Leon stood. His expression was sharp, indicating that he was currently assessing the monster, looking for weak spots..
Sasha swiftly nocked an arrow and whispered a spell under her breath. Mana coalesced around the projectile, forming a visible blue aura along its shaft as she unleashed it.
"[Piercing Bolt]!"
The arrow shot forth, etching itself into the monster’s hide. But the beast barely reacted; it shifted its bulk ever so slightly as if brushing off an annoying insect. It didn’t even bleed.
Sasha cursed under her breath.
Vaelira made her grand entrance next with her mana camera zooming right behind her, capturing even the faintest of motions she made.
With a dramatic wave of her ornate wand, her voice rang out in a commanding tone. "Arise, my warriors. [Summon Legion]!"

The air shimmered in front of her with arcane energies. Mana was sent from her core right into the spell itself, using her wand as a transmitter. Twelve spectral soldiers clad in bronze armor materialized as a result, each wielding large shields and long spears. Their movements were synchronized, making them a disciplined force ready to do their master’s bidding.
Vaelira raised her arms into the air and began making gestures as if she were orchestrating a symphony. She said a single word in her bossy tone: "Engage."
Her order was heard, both by her summoned as well as living minions. The battle erupted in full.

Jack and Leon sprinted straight into the action, with Vaelira’s Roman soldier-themed puppets forming a protective vanguard. The spectral soldiers moved like a well-oiled war machine: with their shields raised in a tight formation, spears lashing out in precise, methodical thrusts.
Kaiden watched the events with a calculating gaze.’Good. They are soaking up the first attacks for us.’
The dune maw, however, was not some mindless beast. It coiled, making its massive, segmented body twist before lunging forward with a speed that defied its bulk.
*Crunch!*

A single sweeping bite snapped through two of the spectral soldiers at once, shattering their forms into fading mana particles. The others didn’t falter nor panic: they closed the gap instantly and stabbed their spears into its rough hide.
It barely noticed their attempts.
The Dune Maw’s hide was thick, hardened by layers of natural armor. The few spear tips that punctured its skin barely sank in, leaving only superficial wounds in their wake.
Then, it unleashed a counterattack.
Its gaping maw split apart even further, revealing countless serrated teeth that churned like a meat grinder.
With a violent whip of its body, the worm lashed out, sending a wave of sand in all directions. The sheer force of the move shattered more of Vaelira’s legion, breaking the formation.
"Ugh! It’s stronger than I thought," Vaelira clicked her tongue. She raised her wand, forming complex gestures. "Use the opportunities presented by my soldiers smarter, you fools!"

Kaiden ignored her screeching, focusing on the chance before him. He advanced under the cover of the soldiers and Jack, who was busy tanking its attacks. The worm lunged again at one of the summoned soldiers, who raised its shield to block.
*Snap!*
The shield caved in instantly, the poor spectral warrior was crushed in the blink of an eye.

But what mattered was that the worm-like monster was momentarily distracted, and Kaiden capitalized on it instantly by swinging his war axe in a devastating arc, aiming for the side of its massive maw.
"[Doom Strike]!"

The blade cut into the softer flesh near the side of its mouth, slicing past the thick exterior. Darkened ichor sprayed from the wound. The damage wasn’t deep enough to cripple it, but it was the first real wound inflicted thus far.
Leon wasn’t far behind Kaiden. Using the same opportunity that was created by their frontline, he stabbed his longsword with all his might, piercing the blade deep into its flesh.
The monster released a furious, ear-piercing shriek that rattled the air, telling them all that damage had been dealt at long last.
That was the exact moment Nyx made her move.
She raised her hand, and a fiery glyph ignited in the air before her as she cast [Astral Summon: Fire].
A large, flaming lance materialized above her. It was a weapon crafted from the very essence of fire itself.

Using [Telekinesis], she hurled it with all her mental strength. It was the mightiest weapon she’d ever summoned thus far, straining her focus. But the Space Valkyrie knew she couldn’t afford to care about such details right now. It was a life-or-death situation.
The fiery lance ripped through the air, striking the Dune Maw dead center.
*Boom!*

chapters.title: Chapter 138: Dune Maw Battle
paragraphs: Flames exploded outward, making the horrible heat of the desert skyrocket for a moment. The beast screeched in great pain, its armored hide was red-hot from the damage it had sustained.

Aria saw the moment and took it. She aimed her staff at the injured monster and closed her eyes for a brief second, focusing her entire existence on gathering mana. It coalesced around her, building up in a concentrated form of destructive lunar energy.
But just as she could release [Lunar Overload], the worm suddenly froze.
Then, in an instant, it burrowed into the sandy ground. A loud rumble sounded as the Dune Maw vanished beneath the sand with great speed. Nothing but a large hole remained in its wake.
For a moment, silence fell over the battlefield. Then, a man who was already mid-attack before the monster made its move tumbled into the hole.

Kaiden’s eyes snapped toward him. The warrior’s fall was not graceful in the slightest—he crashed hard, and his body twisted at an awkward angle. The man struggled to push himself up. He took a great deal of damage from the fall itself.
Their eyes met for a split second. The man reached out toward him. His expression was a desperate plea. "Help... me..."
Kaiden took a step forward.

A blur of movement. That was all he saw before the dune maw exploded forth in a flash, and its massive maw snapped shut around the man in a single, gruesome chomp. Blood splattered across the sand—the man was gone. Only a single boot with his amputated feet still in it was left behind.
The worm’s massive body disappeared back into the dunes in mere seconds. Panic set in, making the remaining fighters scramble, looking around frantically. "Where is it?! Where is it?!"

Kaiden closed his eyes, blocking out the noise, trying to sense the vibrations beneath using his feet. But before he could even begin to focus, the sand erupted once again. It surfaced right next to Sasha.
Her eyes widened in shock. "Aah!" She stumbled back, and her fingers instinctively reached for another arrow, but there was no time.
"RAAAH!"
With a thunderous roar, Jack threw himself at the monster.
A golden glow surrounded him as he shouted, "[Guardian’s Bulwark]!" A defensive barrier manifested around Sasha; the tanker’s spell redirected the worm’s attack toward him instead.
*Boom!*

The worm’s massive jaws crashed into Jack’s barrier, protecting the redheaded archer. The muscled man immediately grunted from the exertion as soon as the resulting damage assaulted him, but Jack held firm, living up to his role as the group’s most talented tanker. He stood in one place, unmoving, with blood seeping through his gritted teeth and nose.

"Leon!" he shouted, and the swordsman immediately jumped into action. A single moment later, the shield vanished from around Sasha, and Leon was already at her location. Lifting the woman into his arms, he bolted away, escaping danger.
"T-thanks..." Sasha muttered with a ghostly pale face that told everyone her life had just flashed in front of her eyes.
Despite the massive amount of damage the dune maw had sustained, its hide still held strong, and its movements, though slightly sluggish now, still carried immense power.
Kaiden’s gaze sharpened, observing each of his Valkyries for a single moment. Then, after ascertaining they were all right, both in mind and body, he turned toward the monster.
"Let’s roll."

He began rushing toward the monster, with Jack and Leon falling into step beside him, and the remaining Legion soldiers charged in as well under Vaelira’s direction. Their shields slammed into the worm’s body, keeping it off balance as Kaiden and Leon unleashed a flurry of attacks.

Kaiden hacked at its flesh, his war axe carving gashes wherever he struck. Leon slashed with the precision one would expect of a trained swordsman, aiming for the wounds Kaiden, in his attacks made with wild abandon, had already inflicted to deepen the damage further. The summoned warriors drove their spears into its hide, adding to the assault.

The dune maw shrieked and thrashed wildly with its massive bulk whipping around in retaliation. Each movement sent shockwaves through the sand, forcing everyone to dodge at a moment’s notice or lose their lives.
Nyx’s eyes narrowed.

One inner look at her body’s condition told the Space Valkyrie she couldn’t summon another massive lance of the proportions she did before. That kind of exertion took too much mana and mental strength. Instead, she adjusted her approach.
With a flick of her wrist, [Astral Summon: Fire] activated once more. This time, a thin, needle-like spear materialized in the air. Less mass. More penetration.
She launched it forward, aiming for its presumed weak spot.
The spear stabbed straight through the worm’s exterior, sinking deep into its body before stopping somewhere within.
The result was not an explosion this time due to the lack of mana investment, but its effects were still resounding.

The Dune Maw convulsed violently, and a deep, guttural screech tore free from its throat. Its movements became erratic, desperate. Flames burned from within as its insides suffered from a fire that refused to die out due to Nyx doing her utmost to keep the flames alive even when her weapon was inside the creature. This, too, required immense focus on her part.
But the monster was finally on its last legs, and Aria was ready. Her staff glowed with a silver shine once again, and this time, [Lunar Overload] had been fully charged.
Since Kaiden, Jack, Leon, and the remaining Legion were all at the front of the beast, attacking its head and midsection, Aria had to adjust her aim toward its tail.
She unleashed the charged attack. A crescent beam of pure lunar energy shot through the air, slamming directly into the Dune Maw’s tail.
*Shing!*

The lower half of the worm was reduced to chunks of flesh and burning meat. The once-massive tail was no longer usable. The beast was crippled. It shrieked as its movements grew even more frantic than before.
A sudden crackling sound filled the air.
"[Lightning Step]."

With lightning surging around her form, Luna moved in an instant, covering the distance in a few moments. She landed on top of the Dune Maw’s head. The Storm Valkyrie knelt and raised her [Stormblade] high.
And then, she plunged it down.
The electrified blade sank straight through the monster’s skull. A burst of lightning erupted from the impact, frying its brain from within.
The dune maw gave one final, deafening cry before it stopped moving. Its massive body lurched forward after the last remnants of life drained from its massive form.
A dust cloud rose from the impact of its collapse; the sheer weight of the beast was more than enough to send tremors through the sand.
[You’ve slain Dune Maw (Level 13). You’ve gained 2200 XP.]
It was a great deal of XP to receive, considering how many of them shared the kill, but instead of rejoicing, Luna stood atop the monster’s unmoving corpse with a troubled expression.

Although she’d made a great move, her mind was still struggling to comprehend what had just transpired before her eyes. Her gaze turned in the direction of Rebecca’s body, with only her upper half remaining. The rest of her was inside the monster’s stomach. The awakened human was no longer emitting any signs of life, not even weak whispers.
A loud wail sounded from a woman who looked just like Rebecca, her twin sister.
"Sister!!!"
She rushed to the body and knelt, clutching her and letting tears paint her sister’s face.
Luna returned to Kaiden and her two friends with a grim expression. None celebrated their victory.

"Let’s check on them..." Nyx said with a sorrowful expression. Seeing such scenes through one’s awakened media platform didn’t do the real thing justice, especially if filmed on the mana cameras and not Kaiden’s [First-Person Camera]. She thought she was ready, but her stomach was churning just as badly as Aria’s and Luna’s.

Kaiden had seen dead people already during his brothel escapade, and he also seemed to have Vespera’s cold blood coursing through his veins, but this loss still saddened him. Killing scum was vastly different from losing one’s allies.

But before they could take more than a few steps, Vaelira called them out with an accusatory tone. "I saw you four cowards! You watched the ongoing scene from a safe distance for many valuable seconds instead of helping your allies!"

But before they could take more than a few steps, Vaelira called them out with an accusatory tone.
"I saw you four cowards!
You watched the ongoing scene from a safe distance for many valuable seconds instead of helping your allies!"

- Lady Leia: God damn. I usually caress my little sis throughout such streams using my Secret Kaiden Stash as assistance material, but I had to pause for the duration of the battle.
- Princeless Princess: You two b*tches are unhinged. Take a chill pill, please.
- Princeless Princess: Excellent job, Valhalla’s Sinners! You’re in the league of respectable combatants now!
- Corn Addict: What a battle...
- Shadow Warrior: Boy, am I glad I grabbed popcorn beforehand.
- Thirsty247: Look, the fangirls are at each other’s throats.
- TouchGrass: When aren’t they?
- Thirsty247: Kaiden senpai is amazing...
- DeleteYuumi: But we gotta admit the ladies more than pulled their weight in this fight.

- Lapdog of the Empress: SUPREME EMPRESS!!!!! This lowly one has been forced onto all fours at the sheer weight of the Empress’s presence! This loyal servant feels unworthy of standing when his Empress is in front of him!
- TouchGrass: She’s not in front of you but on your mind’s screen...

The chat erupted into a myriad of comments. The viewers’ emotions have been reserved throughout the difficult battle, but now that it was finally over, they felt it was time to let it all go. It was a release of tension, a communal catharsis shared by thousands who had been silently gripping their seats, unable to look away.

However, any chatting paused when Vaelira stomped her way toward Kaiden’s group with fury. The blonde woman pointed a finger at him as she accused, "I saw you four cowards! You watched the ongoing scene from a safe distance for many valuable seconds instead of helping your allies!"
- Lady Leia: What nonsense is this ugly whore spouting?
- Kaiden’s Wife: ???
- Princeless Princess: The galls!!

Just like the viewers, the recipients of her words were utterly shocked. If the accusations weren’t ridiculous enough in their lonesome, the fact she started pointing fingers instead of checking on the injured only made it worse. As if this was their cue, Leon, Jack, and Sasha collected themselves and closed in to have the back of their boss.
"What are you even talking about?" Aria asked with a raised eyebrow.
"Don’t you dare pretend to be innocent," Vaelira scoffed before pointing behind herself, right at her camera. "Over ten thousand people saw you stand still, watching the fight. I have the footage."

Nyx’s eyes were reduced to fiery slits, pure anger oozing from her being. "Are you talking about the five seconds we spent strategizing on how to best help our allies instead of rushing in like headless chickens and getting killed in the process?"

Vaelira shook her head, dismissing her point. "Five seconds could’ve saved Ian from his death, even if Rebecca was a lost cause. How can we trust you people if you’re going to hold a team meeting at every emergency? Also, aren’t you awakened combatants? We can’t always afford the luxury of strategizing!"

Kaiden’s gaze turned dark as his eyes interlocked with Vaelira’s. In her eyes, he saw no hatred. She was not even mad at them. This woman was just an opportunistic bitch who used the chance to make herself appear strong in front of her viewers and teammates while also kicking Valhalla’s Sinners down a peg. It wasn’t hard to guess she felt jealous of the girls’ generous genetics. She was ready to do anything to make them look worse than her.

What made their position difficult was that there was a bit of truth to her statement. Yes, they could’ve rushed in with reckless abandon, but Kaiden valued their safety significantly higher than that of his allies. It was logical not to expect mercenaries to sacrifice themselves for their contractors, but calling them out on doing so was also reasonable.

However, Kaiden didn’t believe what they’d done was bad enough to receive this treatment. They rushed in fearlessly after a few short seconds, ready to throw their lives into the mix to bring the monster down. They coordinated with their allies to their utmost ability. It wasn’t like they abandoned their contractors.
A quick look at his chat told him his viewers agreed, but he also noticed that a couple hundred Vaelira fanboys joined in and began talking shit about the four of them being cowards.

Kaiden addressed the accusations while glaring deep into Vaelira’s gaze. "We acted in line with what one might expect of trained professionals. For a brief few moments, we discussed how to best deal with a monster we’ve never even heard of before, let alone had experience fighting. Then, we threw ourselves into the fray, taking on more than our fair share of the danger. If we were to calculate who dealt the most damage, the four of us would outdo the rest of you, members of Nova Circuit."

"Maybe so, but that’s because we were busy tanking its attacks so you could sneak in and attack at the best moments!" Jack shouted while gripping his mace with all his might, making veins pop on his arm.

At this, Luna, who’d been watching the ongoings with a hateful expression, spoke up. But when she did, her expression had shifted, just as her lips turned upward into one of extreme coyness. Her eyes found their way to Vaelira.
"You’re accusing us of very ugly things, Nova Circuit. Since we’re already pointing fingers, allow me to throw my lot in as well," she said, clearing her throat theatrically before continuing.

"We have an A-tier awakened among us low tiers who did nothing but cast a single spell and then make ridiculous hand gestures as if she was in the theatre while shouting orders, making me think she was our basketball coach. Kaiden fought an A-tier combatant in an Awakened Duel in the past—which he won, of course—but his enemy curiously cast many, many spells in the short few seconds it took for Kaiden to pummel the shit out of him. Are you telling me the Puppeteer is such an inferior class to the Archmage that it only has a single good combat spell while the latter has a whole damned arsenal?"
Vaelira’s smile faltered immediately. Her three lackeys tensed, looking at their boss for guidance on how to react.
Hearing their friend’s/girlfriend’s statement, the rest of Valhalla’s Sinners couldn’t help but examine the blonde woman with dismissive eyes.
It was true. She only cast [Summon Legion]. After a mere second, they understood what was going on perfectly well.

Vaelira was conserving her mana. And not just that—she had likely calculated every move she made, from her spell choice to her dramatic finger-pointing. She wasn’t careless. She was cold and calculating.

She was currently on the bench, fulfilling guard duties, after which six hours of hunting awaited her. She knew many of them would share the XP gained from this dune maw kill, so she only did the bare minimum, casting a spell that cost just enough that her reserves would be refilled by the time it was their turn to head out.

"So you’re accusing your leader of nonsense now, huh...? I see how it is... Damned mercs..." Vaelira growled. "My job as team leader is more than casting spells or rushing in like a brute. I’m the centerpiece of the team. Getting clear instructions is how a group with so many fighters can coordinate efficiently."

chapters.title: Chapter 140: Outrage
paragraphs: For a moment, nobody spoke. The only sounds were the wind shifting the desert sands and the distant, muffled sobs of Rebecca’s sister. The tension in the air felt suffocating.
Then, Aria exhaled shakily. Her lips trembled, and her shoulders started shaking uncontrollably.

"You can’t be serious, right? What instructions?" Her usual serene persona was nowhere to be seen. The Moon Valkyrie was just as outraged as her fellow Valkyries. "Your allies whom you trained and grew alongside for four years now were in extreme danger, with two even tragically falling, yet you dare not go all out as our strongest member? And you have the gall to shift the blame around? Have you no shame?!"

By the end, Aria had teared up. Her tender heart was overcome with grief thanks to the losses they suffered and the gruesome pictures of the fallen that were etched deep into her mind. She might not have known anything personal about them, but they were innocent humans nonetheless. All they had ever wanted was to grow stronger and live their lives, and now their journey was cruelly cut short.

"Tch! What a crybaby. This is just ridiculous. I find myself surrounded by clowns instead of dependable allies." With that, the blonde woman turned around on her heels and strode off, leaving stomp marks in the sand.

Now that the tension had eased, Kaiden could relax. With a troubled expression, he moved to embrace his silver-haired lover in a protective hug. That was all Aria needed to have her dams truly opened. The stress and trauma hit her hard, and she was finally allowed to let it all out.

"Let’s take a break," he said to the other ladies, who nodded with similarly grim expressions. They weren’t crying, but their eyes had the same haunted visage to them. Kaiden then reached for Aria’s lower thighs and lifted the woman into his arms. She immediately attached her legs around his waist in a very needy manner.
The four of them quickly found themselves back in their tent. Kaiden sat down on his bed and gestured for Nyx and Luna to sit next to him while the sobbing woman remained in his arms.
"We’re taking a bit of a personal break. Please enjoy the replay of our fight," he said before stopping the live feed of the stream.

Luna sat with her arms wrapped around herself, staring blankly at the floor as she muttered with a pale face, "The harsh reality of our new life, huh..." She played many horror games and saw many corpses in said games, but those games could never do justice to the haunting sight that was Rebecca’s legless torso or her sister’s extreme wailing. It wasn’t just gruesome—it was viscerally real in a way that made her stomach churn.
"Poor woman..." Nyx whispered in a sorrowful tone. Her voice was so soft it barely registered over the stillness in the air.

Kaiden’s arms left Aria’s body to envelop the shoulders of his two other girls, bringing the pair into his sides to make a family hug. His heart was heavy, too. While Kaiden didn’t feel like crying, he was very far from being happy.

Elara, their dutiful aide, loyally followed after them into the tent. Once inside, instead of breaking down despite clear signs of distress being etched all over her youthful features, she fulfilled her servant duties by pouring fresh water into four cups and offering it to them alongside chocolate bars.
"Thank you..." Luna said before she eagerly began munching on her dessert.
"Are you okay?" Kaiden asked, examining Elara’s face while taking a sip of water.
She hesitated. Then, with an almost mechanical nod, she whispered, "Yes... I’ve been trained for this."
Nyx’s sharp eyes caught the lie immediately. She displayed her social butterfly status when she reached out, not for the water, not for the chocolate, but for Elara herself.
Before the girl could react, Nyx pulled her into a hug.

For a second, Elara stiffened. Then, her composure crumbled completely. A small, strangled sound escaped her lips before she buried her face into Nyx’s shoulder and broke down, enveloping the curvaceous woman just like how Aria had embraced Kaiden.

They spent the next hour in silence, doing their best to cope with what had happened. Then, once the girls managed to collect themselves, the group left the tent and saw that the two fallen—or at least what remained of them—were just now being taken outside the portal. Tessa and the rest would take care of the corpses from there.
Kaiden and squad moved outside with them, curious if there was going to be any changes in their strategy.

The dark gazes of the instructors welcomed them, they were watching Vaelira’s stream to remain updated on the ongoings in the dungeon. Contrary to what Kaiden expected, Tessa wasn’t around. It made sense, though. She couldn’t do much here, her time was better used fulfilling her duties as guild leader instead of waiting around.
"Vaelira... I don’t approve of your behavior. Not in the slightest," the grizzly man who sat in front of them back in the minivan growled while eyeing the blonde woman.
She shrugged her shoulders dismissively. "I don’t remember asking for your approval, Has Been."

The man flinched at her harsh and outright insulting words but only gritted his teeth in response. Kaiden observed the bossy bitch’s every move as she turned around and moved back into the dungeon, accompanied by a haughty scoff.

The reasoning behind her choice to become a member of a smaller guild was perfectly depicted through this exchange. She truly was the queen bee who couldn’t be touched, having perfect blackmail material over the entire guild by the mere possibility of her leaving if she didn’t like being here any longer.

Vaelira had likely signed a contract stating she would be a member for X years in exchange for receiving their lengthy and thorough training, but any big guild would happily pay the fines for her if she promised to sign with them instead.

He quickly checked her stream to observe the audience’s response, but to his dismay, he was only seeing disgusting simps glorifying her actions, calling her ’Mistress Vaelira,’ and sending heated emojis.

"... We’re going to look for backup mercenaries, but the chances of us finding them in time is slim," a female instructor said. "The mission has not been canceled. After taking a breather, return to farming XP."
Kaiden and his Valkyries nodded, happy with her instructions. Despite the trauma, they weren’t ready to throw in the towel just yet.

The instructor turned toward the sister of Rebecca, who had been sobbing incessantly up until now while clutching the cold hand of her sister’s corpse. "I’m so sorry for your loss, Dorothy. What do you plan to do?"
The woman’s entire body trembled upon her brain registering the words, and she closed her eyes for a few moments, deliberating what she wanted to do.
By the time she opened them, determination had replaced grief. "I’ll return and demolish the dungeon in Reb’s honor."
The instructor nodded. "I wish you luck."
And just like that, the teams returned to the D-ranked dungeon.

chapters.title: Chapter 141: Chilling in the Oasis
paragraphs: The team that had four members and weren’t Kaiden’s nor Vaelira’s were told to give a member to Dorothy’s team as they had only two members remaining, balancing them out by having three people each.
After that, the hunt resumed. Knowing there were only a few minutes left until their turn came to guard the camp, Kaiden and co didn’t leave.

"Don’t you dare touch our stuff..." Vaelira hissed at the group as she stood, ready to depart. As Jack walked by, he bumped his broad shoulder into Kaiden’s with enough force to make him take a half-step back. The impact was solid, and his heavy armor added extra weight to the motion. It wasn’t an outright hostile attack, but a deliberate move, one of dominance and a silent challenge.
Kaiden didn’t react besides meeting Jack’s eyes and reaching for his axe’s handle. Jack had a smug grin as he continued forward without a word.
"What a lovely bunch..." Nyx said sarcastically before plopping her sensual behind on the table and reaching for a can of Coke.
"Khm!" Aria coughed into her palm while observing the item in the pink-haired beauty’s hands with squinted eyes.

"I sweated out like 50,000 calories in the past six hours, I need to replenish them! This scorching desert sun, combined with my medium armor, is going to be the end of me!" The Space Valkyrie wasn’t ready to heed her personal trainer’s words, not one bit.

"You don’t have to worry; your enormous fat reserves will keep you alive for months. You’re basically a camel," Luna chimed in, receiving a "bleergh!" from Nyx as she pushed her tongue out in response.

Aria ignored the two kittens’ newest jabs. "You’ll just pee those unhealthy sodas out. You need real food, something with protein and carbs to actually restore your energy, not just provide a sugar rush."

Nyx wasn’t receptive to her words of wisdom. "Let’s make a new rule, Princess... I’m truly grateful for your guidance, but so long as we’re inside a dungeon, you cease being my personal trainer. Deal?"
"Same," Luna said while seating herself as far away from Nyx at the table as possible after grabbing a jar of N*tella and a spoon from the box of supplies.

"Haaah..." Aria sighed, but when Kaiden gave her plump butt a playful slap, she smiled happily and decided to go along with the girls’ wishes. She reasoned they had to have a way to deal with the stress of their situation.
She got a box of fruits for herself and Kaiden, which she began feeding her man after seating herself right in his lap.
"Will you join us?" Kaiden asked Elara after grabbing onto Aria’s sensual belly, finding his way expertly under her mage robes to her womb tattoo.
"I can?"

The girl’s dumbfounded expression told them all they needed to know about the customs regarding dungeon aides and relaxation time. She was expected to serve as their waitress while they rested. Not needing such services, especially not from this young girl, they quickly gestured for her to join them.
Elara nodded after a few seconds, with a minute upturn of her lips. "Thank you."
She sat next to Nyx and began devouring a plate of chicken and rice.

The stream was already back in action, and Luna, who was sitting in front of Kaiden, started her own so the ladies could watch him eat... They had about 2000 viewers combined, while Vaelira’s numbers had climbed up to 40,000. "Don’t you dare touch our stuff..." Vaelira hissed at the group as she stood, ready to depart.
As Jack walked by, he bumped his broad shoulder into Kaiden’s with enough force to make him take a half-step back.
The impact was solid, and his heavy armor added extra weight to the motion.
It wasn’t an outright hostile attack, but a deliberate move, one of dominance and a silent challenge.
Kaiden didn’t react besides meeting Jack’s eyes and reaching for his axe’s handle.
Jack had a smug grin as he continued forward without a word.
"What a lovely bunch..." Nyx said sarcastically before plopping her sensual behind on the table and reaching for a can of Coke.
"Khm!" Aria coughed into her palm while observing the item in the pink-haired beauty’s hands with squinted eyes.
"I sweated out like 50,000 calories in the past six hours, I need to replenish them!
This scorching desert sun, combined with my medium armor, is going to be the end of me!" The Space Valkyrie wasn’t ready to heed her personal trainer’s words, not one bit.
"You don’t have to worry; your enormous fat reserves will keep you alive for months.
You’re basically a camel," Luna chimed in, receiving a "bleergh!" from Nyx as she pushed her tongue out in response.
Aria ignored the two kittens’ newest jabs.
"You’ll just pee those unhealthy sodas out.
You need real food, something with protein and carbs to actually restore your energy, not just provide a sugar rush."
Nyx wasn’t receptive to her words of wisdom.
"Let’s make a new rule, Princess...
I’m truly grateful for your guidance, but so long as we’re inside a dungeon, you cease being my personal trainer.
Deal?"
"Same," Luna said while seating herself as far away from Nyx at the table as possible after grabbing a jar of N*tella and a spoon from the box of supplies.
"Haaah..." Aria sighed, but when Kaiden gave her plump butt a playful slap, she smiled happily and decided to go along with the girls’ wishes.
She reasoned they had to have a way to deal with the stress of their situation.
She got a box of fruits for herself and Kaiden, which she began feeding her man after seating herself right in his lap.
"Will you join us?" Kaiden asked Elara after grabbing onto Aria’s sensual belly, finding his way expertly under her mage robes to her womb tattoo.
"I can?"
The girl’s dumbfounded expression told them all they needed to know about the customs regarding dungeon aides and relaxation time.
She was expected to serve as their waitress while they rested.
Not needing such services, especially not from this young girl, they quickly gestured for her to join them.
Elara nodded after a few seconds, with a minute upturn of her lips.
"Thank you."
She sat next to Nyx and began devouring a plate of chicken and rice.
The stream was already back in action, and Luna, who was sitting in front of Kaiden, started her own so the ladies could watch him eat...
They had about 2000 viewers combined, while Vaelira’s numbers had climbed up to 40,000.
Now that she was going to be fighting for the next six hours, her parents ran another bout of ads, and her social media managers made new posts promoting the stream.

chapters.title: Chapter 142: Damned Desert Heat!
paragraphs: Kaiden examined his ladies and noted that the heat was already starting to take its toll. Even with their heightened physical attributes, trekking across loose sand while carrying weapons and armor was pure hell. The desert air was dry enough to sap the moisture straight from their bodies, and each gust of wind sent grains of sand stinging against their skin.
Their boots sank with every step, forcing them to constantly exert more energy just to stay upright. The sun above wasn’t just hot—it was oppressive, like an anvil pressing down on their backs.
"Are we even moving forward?" Nyx muttered while shielding her face from the sun with a gloved hand.
Kaiden glanced over his shoulder. Their starting point was far behind them; the palm trees of the oasis were nowhere in sight. "We are. The pyramid just... doesn’t look to be any closer."
"How very motivating," Luna deadpanned as beads of sweat formed on her temple.

Nearby, the Nova Circuit members weren’t faring any better. Sasha repeatedly wiped her brow while Leon’s steps were growing heavier, and even Jack, the human tank brimming with energy, was slowing down. Vaelira, of course, still carried herself with forced elegance, but Kaiden could see the stiffness in her shoulders.
"Pick up the pace," she snapped at her own teammates. No one answered, but irritation simmered in the group. It was going to be a long day.

"I’m already regretting this... Why did I allow myself to be dragged into a desert dungeon...?" Sasha muttered before gulping a large amount of water down her throat. Her red hair that was previously so vibrant became dull by the thin layer of sand clinging to it.
"You and me both... Fucking hate heat," Leon grumbled.
They had only been marching for a short time, but the heat made it feel much longer.
A loudhuffcame from Jack, who adjusted his heavy armor that seemed more and more adamant about slipping off of his sweaty body. "How the hell are we supposed to fight in these conditions?"
"Something’s coming our way!" Sasha suddenly declared, snapping everyone’s focus forward.

Kaiden narrowed his eyes. At first, he saw nothing. Just more damned sand dunes stretching out endlessly before them. But then, he noticed the disturbance. Based on a thin ripple in the sand, something was moving just beneath the surface.
"Get ready!" he shouted just before the sand erupted.
<Sand Serpent - Level 14>
<Sand Serpent - Level 12>
<Sand Serpent - Level 15>
Three snake-type monsters shot up from below. The creatures slithered on the ground with great speed, and their sand-colored hides made them hard to detect before they struck.
One of the massive beasts lunged at the closest target, Leon.

Accompanied by a sharp curse, the swordsman barely managed to dodge, rolling aside just as the serpent’s maw slammed into the ground where he had stood a mere moment ago. Another burst up near Dorothy. She screamed furiously as she punched it in the face with her brawler gauntlets, but it barely flinched.

Kaiden switched into Wrath Stance and launched himself forward. Warpath carried him straight into the nearest serpent. His axe came down in a crushing arc boosted by [Doom Strike], and he cleaved into the beast’s side, making his target let out a piercing screech. However, it wasn’t dead just yet.
Then came the dune stalkers.

They rushed at them through the sandy dunes, not erupting from the ground this time around. These beings were skeletal, long-limbed creatures with razor-sharp claws, and their hollow eyes shone with greedy hunger that was eager to devour human flesh. Their movements were erratic, lunging at their targets with reckless abandon.
Jack swung his mace just in time, smashing one into the sand before it could tear into him. "Goddamnedthings!" he spat.

Luna repositioned herself so that many monsters lined up for her [Thunder Slash], cutting through multiple stalkers in a single swing of her blade. Nyx followed her lead, using [Astral Summon: Earth] to repeat her strategy of using bludgeon damage against skeletal beings, hurling balls of rock at high speed, shattering bones with every impact.
But the creatures kept on coming.
One managed to claw at Elara’s arm before she could retreat. She yelped, stumbling back as Aria shattered it apart with a swift [Lunar Arc].
"We’re getting surrounded in the backline!" Aria shouted.

Kaiden’s mind raced. They couldn’t afford to get bogged down here. The heat was already killing their stamina; if they let this fight drag out, exhaustion would finish them off even if the monsters didn’t.

"We must move to guard the backline!" he shouted since their so-called captain didn’t seem ready to bark her own instructions. "Don’t get stuck fighting; just clear a path toward them and let our mages and archers deal damage while we fend off the monsters!"

It wasn’t a glorious battle but pure desperation. On the bright side, his strategy had worked. By protecting their backline, they were allowed to attack the monsters without having to fear for their safety.

The ambush lasted longer than Kaiden hoped. By the time the last creature fell, the team was spent. Even though they had survived without a casualty this time around, the real punishment was only just beginning.
The scorching sun showed no mercy whatsoever.

The initial burst of adrenaline from the fight had quickly worn off, leaving them even more drained than before. Every step felt heavier, with every muscle in their bodies screaming for rest. The sand was even hotter now than in the morning, and with their bodies covered in sweat, every gust of wind coated them in sand, making it hard to even exist, let alone breathe.

To people who enjoyed the comforts of 21st-century city life, this was pure torture. While members of Nova Circuit received training against harsh weather conditions, there was only so much such a thing could do to help.

Increasing their Endurance stat was the best bet at combating the stamina loss, while higher Vitality would resist the sun’s scorching. This was why melee combatants were better off than backliners, but then again, they tended to wear heavier gear, which more or less evened the playing field.

Poor Nyx, in her medium armor and heavy Magic investment, got to enjoy the ’best’ of both worlds. If she hadn’t begun putting a few attribute points into her physical stats, she would’ve already collapsed into a wheezing heap of sweat.
Jack let out a groan. "Tell me again why we didn’t wait until sundown?"

Sasha grunted with sheer annoyance; all gratitude for saving her by tanking the dune maw’s bite had left her soul. "We’re racing against the clock, dumbass. Furthermore, these things attack at all hours, and most have a way to find their way around in pitch darkness while we have to rely on shitty lamps."
"Oh... Yeah," the musclebrain nodded, realizing they had less than 48 hours to clear the dungeon.
"You’re drinking too much," Vaelira hissed while watching Nyx down another bottle of water.
Nyx blinked. "I’ve got no choice. I’m about to faint."
"You’ll need it more later. The sun is still traveling upward."

A tense silence hung between them. She wasn’t wrong; if they ran out of water before reaching a safe place, they were as good as dead. But right now, none of them could afford to ration too much, or people would just begin dropping one after the other.

Luna let out an exasperated sigh, not liking the blonde woman’s attitude one bit. Especially because she was consuming water at a very similar rate to Nyx. But, of course, Vaelira was the kind of woman who fully believed in the saying ’rules for thee, not for me.’

"If Nyx faints, we’ll have to carry her. Or are you suggesting we abandon our teammates in their time of need? Oh, of course you are. My bad, for a moment I forgot I was talking to a spineless cunt. "
Sasha hissed with spite, "Shut your trap and keep your eyes ahead!"
"If I wasn’t doing my utmost to conserve my energy..."
Kaiden sighed. This wasn’t going to end well.
They were all running out of patience, becoming easier and easier to irritate.
And the worst of it all? The pyramid still looked just as far away as it had hours ago, serving as the perfect morale breaker.

But, of course, Vaelira was the kind of woman who fully believed in the saying ’rules for thee, not for me.’
"If Nyx faints, we’ll have to carry her.
Or are you suggesting we abandon our teammates in their time of need?
Oh, of course you are.
My bad, for a moment I forgot I was talking to a spineless cunt.
Sasha hissed with spite, "Shut your trap and keep your eyes ahead!"
"If I wasn’t doing my utmost to conserve my energy..."
Kaiden sighed.
This wasn’t going to end well.
They were all running out of patience, becoming easier and easier to irritate.
And the worst of it all?
The pyramid still looked just as far away as it had hours ago, serving as the perfect morale breaker.

chapters.title: Chapter 143: Tense Silence
paragraphs: More hours passed.
The air shimmered from the overwhelming heat, turning the sand beneath their feet into an endless sea of golden death. Walking on it felt like traversing on a large, heated cooking pan.

Sweat oozed down everyone’s faces, with their bodies aching from the sheer effort walking under the merciless sun took. Even the most physically capable among them felt it—the slow, creeping exhaustion clawing into their very bones.
The accursed waiting only made things worse.
There had been no attacks for hours. No sand worms, no undead horrors, nothing. Just silence. The longer it stretched, the more unbearable it became.
No one trusted it.

Kaiden felt his grip tighten on his war axe. His instincts screamed at him. This wasn’t right. It wasn’t mercy but a setup, made to lull them into a false sense of safety. However, he couldn’t do anything about it. The only thing that could help was forcing whatever monster he was sure to be laying an ambush for them out into the open, but he had no means to do so.
Just as he was cursing under his breath,ithappened.
It started with a single, quiet thump.
Someone collapsed mid-step, hitting the sand face-first. At first, no one reacted. Everyone was too drained to process it. Then, someone turned toward the direction of the sound. "Hey... you okay?"
No response.
They rushed over, flipping the man onto his back. His eyes were wide, his lips parted, but he wasn’t breathing. A faint trail of blood leaked from his mouth.
Kaiden’s heart pounded as his gaze swept lower. There, embedded in his neck, was a tiny black dart.
"Ambush!"
Panic exploded in the group. Some ducked, others scrambled for cover that didn’t exist. The vast, open desert provided no place to hide.
"Where’s it coming from?!" Leon snarled, unsheathing his longsword.
"What even is it in the first place?!" Jack screamed after letting off a cursing spree.
Another body hit the sand. Then a third.
They were being picked off.
Kaiden’s mind worked at full speed. Snipers? No, that didn’t fit. The darts were too small, too crude.
His eyes snapped to the dunes in the long distance, and then he saw it.
<Pharaoh’s Fang - level 14>
<Pharaoh’s Fang - level 16>
<Pharaoh’s Fang - level 13>
"There! Small insects!"
Noticing they were found out, the creatures burst forth from below the sands they used as their cover, with only their little dart-like tails and eyes being visible.
Then, they began rushing backward while aiming their stingers at the group, doing their utmost to keep the distance between them and the awakened, who was already rushing to crush them.

Once they knew where to look, the faster combatants could dodge, and even the slower ones, like Jack, had enough presence to raise their shields to block the incoming darts. These monsters proved to be one-trick ponies, only proficient at stealthy sniper attacks.

After Kaiden and the rest reached them, they crumbled apart from even weak slashes or projectiles sent from the backline. But the damage was already done. Three people lay motionless in the sand. They never even got to fight for their lives.

The last pharaoh’s fang twitched as it was squished to death with Jack’s hammer, but no one cheered. They were breathing too hard, some holding their hands to their necks, checking for dart wounds that weren’t there. Paranoia had officially settled in.
Then, a low howl echoed in the distance.
At first, it sounded like the wind.
Then it grew.
Kaiden turned, and his stomach sank as he saw the wall of rolling sand approaching them fast.
"Sandstorm!"
Before anyone could mount a response, it slammed into them.

The world turned into a suffocating blur of gold and brown. Visibility dropped to nothing. Kaiden couldn’t even see Luna, who had been standing next to him a second ago. "Kai!!" Following her voice, he reached out to the Storm Valkyrie, and his grip found its mark.

He hugged the girl close, doing his utmost to protect the both of them while gritting his teeth with fright, not daring to imagine how his other ladies might be faring without him. Kaiden knew it was utterly impossible to find them in these conditions. All he could do was trust them and hope for the best. This made it all the worse.
Voices shouted, muffled and distant. Then, screams. Someone had been visibly ripped from the ground, thrown into the air by the sandstorm. Someone else screamed. Then another. And then, silence.
Kaiden immediately snapped his head around, searching for Nyx and Aria. He couldn’t care less about anyone else.

His heart skipped a beat when his eyes landed on the pair, who was caught by none other than Elara. The girl had a lot of Strength stat to her name. She used her hands to grab onto the relatively physically weak girls, not letting the sandstorm drag them away.
At that moment, the young girl had earned Valhalla’s Sinners’ gratitude.
By the time the storm passed, the other survivors stood in place, blinking at the emptiness around them.
They did a headcount only to find that three more were missing. No bodies. No tracks. Just ’puff’ and they were gone, likely thrown far away by the storm.

After Kaiden embraced each of his girls and thanked Elara—who refused to accept his gratitude, saying she was just doing her part—the journey resumed. A brief few sentences were exchanged between the squad to note how brutal this dungeon turned out to be and that they were wholly underestimating it. But then, they didn’t speak much after that. No one had the energy.
They pressed forward, step by agonizing step.
A few hours later, someone gasped.
"Look!"
Everyone’s heads snapped up. A new sight came into vision. It wasn’t just a trick of the heat; they were sure of it. Water... An oasis stood before them.
A perfect, blue pool glistened under the sun. At the tantalizing sight, the sole remaining member from Dorothy’s original team broke into a sprint.
"Wait!" the brawler shouted, but he didn’t stop. He ran with full force, sand kicking up behind him. His crazed eyes were wide with desperate thirst.
